Now the thing is: sometimes avoidance is productive, and you asked earlier about other mental illnesses that can be affected by this predictive thing, and depression is really one of them. You can kind of think of depression as being “let’s curl up in a dark room,” like a strategy of that. And, you know, people argue that, evolutionarily, that may be why we have this thing that we call depression in the sense that if you’re failing, sometimes withdrawing and, like, getting out of the situation is a good idea. And if you have a mechanism to make that happen, if you’re, like, failing, like, socially or in whatever ways, then that could be productive. However, if you get stuck there, then it becomes unproductive, and obviously the feelings of it can just escalate such that it’s very difficult to escape from without, you know, chemical or therapeutic help.
paras.zh: Szalavitz：你可以把它想象成一名消防员，他经常进入这些非常紧张、危险的情况，并经常应对极端压力。或者你可以说，嗯，一个科学家，你知道，一个每天都在挑战他们看待世界的方式的人，就像将想法进行各种测试之类的。所以它看起来可能就像一个真正试图避免过多回避这个世界的人。现在的问题是：有时回避是有成效的，您之前询问过可能受这种预测性影响的其他精神疾病，而抑郁症确实是其中之一。你可以把抑郁症想象成“让我们蜷缩在一个黑暗的房间里”，就像这样的一种策略。而且，你知道，人们认为，从进化的角度来看，这可能就是为什么我们会患上抑郁症，因为如果你失败了，有时退缩，比如摆脱困境是个好主意。如果你有一个机制来实现这一点，如果你在社交方面或以任何方式失败，那么这可能是富有成效的。然而，如果你被困在那里，那么它就会变得毫无成效，而且显然它的感觉只会升级，以至于在没有化学或治疗帮助的情况下很难逃脱。

paras.en: Feltman: So can understanding the brain as a prediction engine actually help us cope better with uncertainty? Your piece certainly had a very compelling narrative lead that got into this a little bit. So maybe you could start by sharing that with our listeners.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：那么将大脑理解为预测引擎实际上可以帮助我们更好地应对不确定性吗？你的作品肯定有一个非常引人注目的叙事线索，其中涉及到这一点。所以也许你可以先与我们的听众分享这一点。

paras.en: Szalavitz: When I was interviewing the authors of the paper that described those various phenotypes, they had just survived the Eaton Fire in Los Angeles, and they had been working on the paper during that, and the fire actually threatened their homes very significantly, and they had to, like, evacuate in a smoky, messy, scary hell.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：当我采访描述这些不同表型的论文的作者时，他们刚刚在洛杉矶伊顿火灾中幸存下来，在那段时间他们一直在写论文，而火灾实际上对他们的家园造成了非常严重的威胁，他们不得不在烟雾缭绕、混乱不堪、可怕的地狱中撤离。

paras.en: And to top it all off, one of the co-authors was injured in a childhood diving accident, and so he is quadriplegic, and he uses a wheelchair, and the mobility van that transports his wheelchair was undergoing service. So he couldn’t get into his wife’s car, and they had to leave, and he had to, like, drive his electric wheelchair through, you know, the falling debris and the howling winds and the smoke and all of that to get to a place where a vehicle could get to that would be capable of him getting picked up.
paras.zh: 最糟糕的是，其中一位合著者在童年的一次潜水事故中受伤，因此他四肢瘫痪，他使用轮椅，而运送他轮椅的流动货车正在接受维修。所以他无法进入他妻子的车，他们必须离开，他必须驾驶他的电动轮椅，穿过掉落的碎片、呼啸的风和烟雾以及所有这些，才能到达一个车辆可以到达的地方，这样他就可以被接走。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. That’s a tough one for the old prediction engine, I got to say. [Laughs.]
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。我不得不说，这对于旧的预测引擎来说是一项艰巨的任务。 [笑。]

paras.en: Szalavitz: No, exactly. And so that was why, like, when I was interviewing them, Laura Harrison brought it up because she was like, “This got put to the test for us very seriously, you know, in these circumstances.”
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：不，完全正确。这就是为什么，当我采访他们时，劳拉·哈里森（Laura Harrison）提出了这个问题，因为她说，“你知道，在这种情况下，这对我们来说是非常严肃的考验。”

paras.en: And so, you know, I wasn’t originally gonna write about any of that. I was just writing about the paper, and so then I had the anecdote that would, like, allow us to get into, you know, the very real-world implications of how we manage uncertainty. And, you know, they were talking about, while they were in that moment, like, thinking about these ideas and thinking about, like, “Okay, well, how do I respond in a proentropic or at least resilient way?” and, you know, “How do I manage the odds of, like, is it safer to stay or go?”
paras.zh: 所以，你知道，我本来不想写这些的。我只是在写这篇论文，然后我就得到了一个轶事，它可以让我们了解我们如何管理不确定性的现实世界的影响。而且，你知道，他们当时正在谈论，就像思考这些想法并思考，“好吧，好吧，我如何以亲熵或至少有弹性的方式做出反应？”而且，你知道，“我如何管理诸如留下或离开更安全之类的可能性？”

paras.en: And so it was really fascinating to think about that. And when you do that, the other thing that becomes very clear is that managing your emotions is very important because your emotions are kind of there, they’re kind of decision-making algorithms to, like, guide you when under uncertainty, right? Like, this has worked in the past, so this will feel good. This doesn’t, so it won’t, right? So you have to be aware of those influences and whether they are guiding you in the right direction or not. And you also have to be aware that, like, when your brain is flooded with stress hormones, you are not thinking about the future the way you ordinarily do because you’re very narrowed in on where you are now, which is important when you’re getting out of a fire.
paras.zh: 所以想到这一点真的很有趣。当你这样做时，另一件事变得非常清楚，管理你的情绪非常重要，因为你的情绪就在那里，它们是一种决策算法，可以在不确定的情况下指导你，对吗？就像，这在过去已经奏效了，所以这会感觉很好。这不会，所以不会，对吧？所以你必须意识到这些影响以及它们是否引导你走向正确的方向。而且你还必须意识到，当你的大脑充满压力荷尔蒙时，你不会像平常那样思考未来，因为你的注意力非常集中在你现在所处的位置，这在你逃离火灾时很重要。

paras.en: But it means that you’re not going to be at your most creative or at your most able to deal with abstraction. And so, you know, this is why, like, in national emergencies, it’s so difficult to manage because we just freak out. [Laughs.] I mean, I sort of feel like what happened, you know, with the pandemic is that that massive social stress moved everybody a notch higher away from planning and abstraction and deeper thought and into a more reactive and often aggressive, unfortunately, mode. So kind of understanding all of this in this context is really useful when you want to try to, like, cope with either on a personal or a, you know, political level the challenges that we are facing now.
paras.zh: 但这意味着你不会发挥出最大的创造力或最有能力处理抽象。所以，你知道，这就是为什么，就像在国家紧急情况下，管理如此困难，因为我们只是吓坏了。 [笑]我的意思是，我觉得，你知道，随着这场大流行病的发生，巨大的社会压力让每个人都远离了计划、抽象和更深入的思考，不幸的是，进入了一种更加反应性、往往更具攻击性的模式。因此，当您想要尝试在个人或政治层面应对我们现在面临的挑战时，在这种情况下理解所有这些确实非常有用。

paras.en: Feltman: Well, and speaking of that shift in the wrong direction that I think we all feel very aware of, you made the point that these phenotypes aren’t really fixed, and that we can change the way our prediction engines work. Could you talk a little bit about how that’s possible?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：嗯，说到错误方向的转变，我认为我们都非常清楚，你指出这些表型并不是真正固定的，我们可以改变预测引擎的工作方式。您能谈谈这怎么可能吗？

paras.en: Szalavitz: So obviously, we are limited, to some extent, by our temperament. Like, I’m never gonna be the chillest person in the world. That probably will not happen. But we can move away from our default responses toward, if they have become dysfunctional, toward more appropriate and, and helpful ones. And you do that by explicitly facing it—not in a way like tough love or force or any of that. And this is a lot of what cognitive-behavioral therapy is. It’s like, you know, “Okay, I walk into the room; I assume they hate me.” That’s my brain doing the assumption. It’s not them doing anything. So I have to be aware of that, and I have to say, “Well, what’s the evidence for my belief that they’re going to hate me?” And there probably isn’t any. And so I need to, like, let go of that and just go into the room with a better expectation. When you face these kinds of things, you have to not assume your perception is automatically correct or real, and you have to assume that it’s provisional.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：很明显，我们在某种程度上受到我们的气质的限制。就像，我永远不会成为世界上最冷的人。这可能不会发生。但是，如果我们的默认反应变得功能失调，我们可以摆脱默认反应，转向更合适、更有帮助的反应。你可以通过明确地面对它来做到这一点——而不是以严厉的爱或强制或任何其他方式。这就是认知行为疗法的大部分内容。就像，你知道，“好吧，我走进房间；我认为他们恨我。”这是我的大脑在做这个假设。不是他们在做任何事情。所以我必须意识到这一点，我必须说，“那么，有什么证据可以证明我相信他们会恨我呢？”可能没有。所以我需要放下这些，带着更好的期望走进房间。当你面对这类事情时，你不能假设你的感知自动是正确的或真实的，你必须假设它是暂时的。

paras.en: And the more you can, like, expect surprise and, you know, work toward having the surprises ideally be pleasant ones, then you can get better at managing the whole thing—because it’s kind of amazing how much stuff is, like, building muscle, where it’s just, like, you start with, like, the lower weights, and you suck, and you’re bad at it, and then you repeat it, and then you actually see that you can really get a lot stronger, right? So this is true whether it’s managing stress or, you know, learning anything. But what we tend to do is, sort of, push people into the deep end, and then they’re like, “Well, I can’t do this. I’m bad at this.” It’s like, if you, for your first [time] trying to lift weights, [you] tried to lift 300 pounds, you would not succeed, and you would probably injure yourself, right? But you can, I can attest, build up to this by a lot of practice over many, many years. When it is stress or when it is, like, some of our psychological tendencies, a groove gets worn into your brain because it’s easier and because otherwise we couldn’t possibly handle the complexity of the world.
paras.zh: 你越能期待惊喜，并且，你知道，努力让惊喜最好是令人愉快的，那么你就能更好地管理整个事情——因为令人惊奇的是，有多少东西，比如，锻炼肌肉，就像，你从较低的重量开始，你很糟糕，你不擅长，然后你重复它，然后你实际上发现你真的可以变得更强壮，对吧？所以无论是管理压力还是学习任何东西都是如此。但我们倾向于做的就是，把人们推入深渊，然后他们就会说，“好吧，我做不到。我不擅长这个。”就像，如果你第一次尝试举重，你尝试举起 300 磅，你不会成功，而且你可能会受伤，对吗？但我可以证明，你可以通过多年的大量实践来实现这一目标。当压力或我们的某些心理倾向时，你的大脑就会陷入困境，因为这样更容易，否则我们就无法应对世界的复杂性。

paras.en: So one of the interesting things and implications of the predictive brain stuff is that if you can increase brain plasticity, you can interrupt some of these patterns and help people predict in a more functional way. And it’s really interesting to me that everything, with a few minor exceptions, that has antidepressant effects, whether it’s, like, SSRIs [selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors], exercise, ECT [electroconvulsive therapy], psychedelics, all of these things increase plasticity. And psychedelics do it in an especially interesting way because they seem to open up windows of plasticity that are only open at certain points during development. And so I find that fascinating.
paras.zh: 因此，预测性大脑的有趣之处和意义之一是，如果你可以增加大脑的可塑性，你就可以中断其中一些模式并帮助人们以更实用的方式进行预测。对我来说，真正有趣的是，除了少数例外，所有东西都具有抗抑郁作用，无论是 SSRI（选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂）、运动、ECT（电休克疗法）、迷幻药，所有这些东西都会增加可塑性。致幻剂以一种特别有趣的方式做到这一点，因为它们似乎打开了可塑性之窗，而这些可塑性之窗仅在发育过程中的某些时刻打开。所以我觉得这很有趣。

paras.en: Feltman: Well, thank you so much for coming on to talk to us. Your article was fascinating and it was great talking to you.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：非常感谢您接受我们的采访。你的文章很有趣，和你交谈很愉快。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. You can read Maia’s feature online or in the latest issue of Scientific American, which is on newsstands now. We’ll be back on Monday with our weekly science news roundup.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。您可以在线阅读 Maia 的专题报道，也可以在报摊上最新一期的《科学美国人》中阅读。我们将于周一带着每周科学新闻综述回来。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great weekend!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。周末愉快！

articles.title: Japan’s MMX mission will reveal the origins of weird Martian moons

paras.en: Roaring away on top of a tongue of flame, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s (JAXA’s) ambitious Martian Moons Exploration (MMX) spacecraft launched on its way to Mars on October 19. Its mission: to study the Martian moons Phobos and Deimos, setting down on the surface of the former (along with a small rover) and even returning a 10-gram sample of Phobian material to Earth for later study.
paras.zh: 日本宇宙航空研究开发机构 (JAXA) 雄心勃勃的火星卫星探索 (MMX) 航天器在火焰之上呼啸而过，于 10 月 19 日发射升空，前往火星。它的任务是：研究火星卫星火卫一和火卫二，降落在火卫一的表面（连同一个小型漫游车），甚至将 10 克的火卫一物质样本带回地球供以后研究。

paras.en: The two tiny moons—Phobos is a lumpy space potato that is about 26 kilometers in length, and Deimos is an oddly shaped rock that is about 16 km long—were discovered in 1877 but still hold many mysteries tight. Despite close-up images taken of both by various Mars missions over the decades, there is much we still don’t understand about them, even basics such as how they formed. In fact, this is such a big question that answering it is actually MMX’s primary goal.
paras.zh: 这两颗小卫星——火卫一是一块长约 26 公里的块状太空马铃薯，火卫二是一块形状奇特的岩石，长约 16 公里——于 1877 年被发现，但仍然有许多未解之谜。尽管几十年来各种火星任务拍摄了它们的特写图像，但我们仍然对它们有很多不了解，甚至包括它们如何形成等基础知识。事实上，这是一个很大的问题，回答这个问题实际上是 MMX 的首要目标。

paras.en: I’m excited about this mission! MMX will take a year to voyage to the Red Planet and, once there, will slip into an orbit around Mars that will keep it close to Phobos. It will map Phobos’s surface to measure the moon’s shape and scout for potential landing sites (and will also occasionally observe Deimos from a distance). Once engineers back on Earth choose an appropriate spot on Phobos, MMX will deploy a rover to roam the surface, and soon thereafter, the mission’s main spacecraft will touch down. It will collect a small sample of the surface regolith—the powdery material made from rocks pulverized by meteorite impacts and thermal weathering—and eventually blast off into space once again. The plan is to then fly by Deimos for some close-up observations and to subsequently head back to Earth to return the surface sample in 2031.
paras.zh: 我对这个任务感到很兴奋！ MMX 将花费一年时间航行到这颗红色星球，到达那里后，将滑入围绕火星的轨道，使其靠近火卫一。它将绘制火卫一的表面地图，以测量月球的形状并寻找潜在的着陆点（偶尔也会从远处观察火卫二）。一旦工程师返回地球，在火卫一上选择了合适的地点，MMX 将部署一个漫游车在地表漫游，不久之后，任务的主航天器将着陆。它将收集一小部分表面风化层样本（由陨石撞击和热风化粉碎的岩石制成的粉末状物质），并最终再次飞入太空。计划随后飞越火卫二进行近距离观察，并于 2031 年返回地球返回表面样本。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The rover’s design is pretty clever. It’s a joint effort by France’s National Center for Space Studies (CNES) and the German Aerospace Center (DLR). Called Idefix (after the dog in the French Asterix comic), it has a mass of about 24 kilograms. It’s not much bigger than a large shoebox, although, once the solar panels extend, it will span just more than a meter across.
paras.zh: 火星车的设计非常巧妙。这是法国国家空间研究中心 (CNES) 和德国航空航天中心 (DLR) 的共同努力。它被称为 Idefix（以法国 Asterix 漫画中的狗命名），质量约为 24 公斤。它并不比一个大鞋盒大多少，不过，一旦太阳能电池板延伸，它的跨度将只有一米多。

paras.en: The deployment is pretty gutsy—if successful, it will make Phobos the smallest body ever visited by a wheeled rover. It starts with MMX slowing to a stop about 40 to 100 meters above Phobos and then releasing Idefix. From there, the moon’s weak gravity (only about a thousandth as strong as Earth’s) will pull the rover slowly down; the descent could last several minutes even from such a low height. The impact will be gentle, probably less than one meter per second, roughly human walking speed.
paras.zh: 这次部署相当大胆——如果成功，火卫一将成为轮式漫游车访问过的最小天体。首先，MMX 减速至火卫一上方约 40 至 100 米处停止，然后释放 Idefix。从那里，月球的微弱引力（只有地球引力的千分之一左右）会将火星车缓慢地拉下来；即使从如此低的高度下降也可能持续几分钟。影响将是温和的，可能不到每秒一米，大约是人类行走的速度。

paras.en: After that, the locomotion system is designed to flip the rover upright no matter how it lands, putting the wheels down so it can move. Even that is tricky; Idefix will weigh only about 15 grams, or roughly half an ounce, on Phobos! A house sparrow on Earth weighs twice as much. Idefix is designed to measure the moon’s surface temperature and mineralogy, but it will also snap pictures of its wheel tracks on Phobos to better understand the cohesion strength and size of the regolith grains.
paras.zh: 之后，移动系统的设计目的是，无论漫游车如何着陆，它都会将其翻转直立，将轮子放下，以便它可以移动。即使这样也很棘手；在火卫一上，Idefix 的重量仅为约 15 克，即约半盎司！地球上的麻雀的重量是地球上的两倍。 Idefix 旨在测量月球表面温度和矿物学，但它也会拍摄火卫一上的轮轨照片，以更好地了解风化层颗粒的内聚强度和大小。

paras.en: So why is there interest in the Martian moons? Mostly it’s because their origin story is so baffling.
paras.zh: 那么为什么人们对火星卫星感兴趣呢？主要是因为他们的起源故事太令人费解了。

paras.en: Mars sits on the inner edge of the main asteroid belt, so some scientists have proposed that these wee moons are captured asteroids. One point in this idea’s favor is that the compositions of both moons resemble those of common asteroids.
paras.zh: 火星位于主小行星带的内缘，因此一些科学家提出这些小卫星是捕获的小行星。对这个想法有利的一点是，两颗卫星的成分都类似于普通小行星的成分。

paras.en: It’s difficult, however, for a planet to grab a passing rock and keep it; orbital mechanics dictate that an asteroid must shed a lot of velocity in order for Mars to ensnare it. Such an object would have to be on a fantastically lucky trajectory to, say, dip down and drag through the upper Martian atmosphere to slow to just the right speed for capture.
paras.zh: 然而，对于行星来说，抓住并保留经过的岩石是很困难的。轨道力学规定，小行星必须失去很大的速度才能被火星捕获。这样的物体必须处于极其幸运的轨道上，比如说，向下倾斜并拖过火星上层大气层，减慢到适合捕获的速度。

paras.en: It’s far easier, though, if the incoming asteroid is binary: two rocks in orbit around each other. In that case, one of the pair falls into orbit while the other is ejected from the system and carries away the excess energy. That means there must have been two separate events to snag both moons; their orbits are very different, with Phobos a mere 6,000 km above the Martian surface and Deimos a little more than 20,000 km up, so they were unlikely to have been captured together.
paras.zh: 不过，如果传入的小行星是双星的：两块岩石在轨道上相互围绕，那就容易得多。在这种情况下，一对中的一个落入轨道，而另一个则从系统中弹出并带走多余的能量。这意味着必须有两个独立的事件才能捕获这两个卫星；它们的轨道非常不同，火卫一距离火星表面仅 6,000 公里，而火卫二距离火星表面略高于 20,000 公里，因此它们不太可能被一起捕获。

paras.en: Also, both moons have circular orbits directly over Mars’s equator, whereas captured asteroids would be expected to fall along more elongated trajectories around the planet. Such highly elliptical orbits could have been circularized via atmospheric drag and tidal forces from Mars acting on the moons. But this process takes so long (billions of years) that it’s not clear that enough time would have elapsed for Deimos to have settled onto its current path that way.
paras.zh: 此外，两颗卫星都有直接越过火星赤道的圆形轨道，而捕获的小行星预计会沿着更细长的轨道落在火星周围。这种高度椭圆的轨道可能是通过火星作用在卫星上的大气阻力和潮汐力而变成圆形的。但这个过程需要很长时间（数十亿年），以至于尚不清楚火卫二是否需要足够的时间才能以这种方式走上目前的道路。

paras.en: Another possibility is that a large asteroid impact on Mars could have thrown material into space that then coalesced as the moons. This mechanism has precedent; our own moon came to be that way when a small planet (about the size of Mars, ironically enough) slammed into Earth not long after the formation of our world,: the impact ejected huge amounts of rock that rapidly condensed to form our faithful companion.
paras.zh: 另一种可能性是，小行星对火星的巨大撞击可能会将物质抛入太空，然后合并成卫星。该机制已有先例；当我们的世界形成后不久，一颗小行星（讽刺的是，大约与火星大小相当）撞击地球时，我们的月球就变成了这样：撞击喷射出大量岩石，这些岩石迅速凝结成我们忠实的伴侣。

paras.en: Indeed, there are hints that, in some ways, the Martian moons’ compositions resemble that of the Red Planet. But if they formed from the same event, why are they in such different orbits? Perhaps many such objects were formed from the event, and the current moons are the only survivors. A more recent hypothesis is that one moon formed (either together with Mars or from a later impact) but was itself blown apart by an impact to create the extant pair; this idea can explain the circular equatorial orbits, as well as the current differences in their orbital heights.
paras.zh: 事实上，有迹象表明，在某些方面，火星卫星的成分与红色星球的成分相似。但如果它们是由同一事件形成的，为什么它们的轨道如此不同呢？也许许多这样的物体是由这次事件形成的，而当前的卫星是唯一的幸存者。最近的一个假设是，一颗卫星形成了（与火星一起形成或由后来的撞击形成），但它本身被撞击炸碎，形成了现存的一对卫星。这个想法可以解释圆形赤道轨道，以及它们当前轨道高度的差异。

paras.en: Phobos is lower-density than expected for a solid rock, so it’s likely to be at least partially a rubble pile, composed of countless smaller rocks held together by their mutual gravity. Many, if not most, smaller asteroids are rubble piles, and we’re still not completely sure how this happens. It almost certainly results from impacts, with the leading candidate being a smashup energetic enough to shatter the asteroid but not quite sufficient to dissipate it. Afterward, the broken pieces fall back together via gravity. If this is true for Phobos, MMX will tell scientists a lot about how it’s changed over time.
paras.zh: 火卫一的密度比固体岩石的预期要低，因此它可能至少部分是碎石堆，由无数较小的岩石通过相互重力结合在一起组成。许多（如果不是大多数）较小的小行星都是碎石堆，我们仍然不完全确定这是如何发生的。它几乎肯定是由撞击造成的，主要候选者是一颗粉碎性小行星，其能量足以粉碎小行星，但不足以消散它。之后，破碎的碎片通过重力重新聚集在一起。如果火卫一确实如此，MMX 将告诉科学家很多关于它如何随时间变化的信息。

paras.en: There have been previous attempts to send dedicated spacecraft to Phobos (such as the former Soviet Union’s Phobos 1 and 2 missions and the Russian-Chinese mission Phobos-Grunt), but they all failed in different ways to get there. In fact, many missions to Mars have failed, prompting the dark joke in the space community that a monster on Mars called the Great Galactic Ghoul was eating them. Mind you, Phobos and Deimos are named after the minor gods of fear and terror, both sons of Ares!
paras.zh: 此前曾有过向火卫一发送专用航天器的尝试（例如前苏联的火卫一号和火卫二号任务以及俄罗斯和中国的火卫一号任务），但都以不同的方式未能到达那里。事实上，许多火星任务都失败了，这在太空界引发了一个黑色笑话：火星上有一个叫做“银河食尸鬼”的怪物正在吃掉他们。请注意，火卫一和火卫二是以恐惧和恐怖的小神命名的，他们都是阿瑞斯的儿子！

paras.en: I hope MMX has more luck. It’s well past time humanity was successful in sending a dedicated probe to these weird little Martian moons. The images and data will be wonderful, and hopefully many mysteries will be unraveled—as inevitably more will pop up. That’s science, and that’s why we explore. There are always more fun things to discover.
paras.zh: 希望MMX能有更多的运气。人类早就成功地向这些奇怪的小火星卫星发射了专用探测器。图像和数据将会非常精彩，希望许多谜团能够被解开——因为不可避免地会出现更多谜团。这就是科学，这就是我们探索的原因。总是有更多有趣的事情有待发现。

articles.title: How exposing yourself to your fears can tame your anxiety

paras.en: The first time Kevin MacKenzie scrambled up a slide, a steep stretch of rock exposed by weather and geological forces, in the Adirondack Mountains, he swore he’d never do it again.
paras.zh: 凯文·麦肯齐 (Kevin MacKenzie) 第一次在阿迪朗达克山脉 (Adirondack Mountains) 攀爬滑梯时，他发誓再也不会这么做了。滑梯是一片因天气和地质作用而暴露在外的陡峭岩石。

paras.en: But the 56-year-old did do it again—and again and again. After multiple climbs, he became more comfortable, and today he even helps rescue other climbers who find themselves stranded midway up a rock face.
paras.zh: 但这位 56 岁的老人确实一次又一次地这么做了。经过多次攀登后，他变得更加自在，今天他甚至帮助营救其他发现自己被困在岩壁中途的登山者。

paras.en: What MacKenzie has achieved is similar to a clinical technique called exposure therapy, a research-backed approach to taming a multitude of anxieties by exposing a person to their fears in a controlled way. “My fear never disappears,” MacKenzie says, “but repeated exposure has taught me I will have similar outcomes every time.”
paras.zh: 麦肯齐所取得的成就类似于一种称为暴露疗法的临床技术，这是一种由研究支持的方法，通过以受控的方式让一个人暴露在恐惧之中来抑制多种焦虑。 “我的恐惧永远不会消失，”麦肯齐说，“但反复的接触告诉我，每次都会有类似的结果。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: A DIY approach to exposure can work in some circumstances, says Jordan Conrad, a psychotherapist and director of Lexington Park Psychotherapy in New York City. “If you are clear about your fears and approach it seriously and carefully, you can try it on your own,” he says. “But sometimes a clinician is necessary to understand what’s at the bottom of an anxiety.”
paras.zh: 纽约市列克星敦公园心理治疗中心的心理治疗师兼主任乔丹·康拉德 (Jordan Conrad) 表示，在某些情况下，DIY 的暴露方法可能会奏效。 “如果你清楚自己的恐惧，并认真、仔细地对待它，你可以自己尝试一下，”他说。 “但有时需要临床医生来了解焦虑的根源。”

paras.en: For example, a person could have extreme anxiety about dating and might decide to expose their fears with a constant roster of romantic rendezvous. “But underneath that may be fear of abandonment,” Conrad says, “so that’s a wrong use” of exposure therapy.
paras.zh: 例如，一个人可能对约会极度焦虑，并可能决定通过不断的浪漫约会来暴露自己的恐惧。 “但其背后可能是对被遗弃的恐惧，”康拉德说，“所以这是暴露疗法的错误使用”。

paras.en: Working with a trained therapist can help people to both drill down to the cause of their anxiety or fear and develop mechanisms for calming themselves down.
paras.zh: 与训练有素的治疗师合作可以帮助人们深入了解焦虑或恐惧的原因，并建立让自己平静下来的机制。

paras.en: “We know that what exacerbates anxiety is avoidance,” explains Alissa Jerud, a licensed clinical psychologist and clinical assistant professor at the University of Pennsylvania. “Exposure therapy helps develop new, healthier relationships with your anxieties by breaking the avoidance habit.”
paras.zh: “我们知道，回避会加剧焦虑，”宾夕法尼亚大学临床心理学家兼临床助理教授艾丽莎·杰鲁德 (Alissa Jerud) 解释道。 “暴露疗法可以打破回避习惯，帮助你与焦虑建立新的、更健康的关系。”

paras.en: Traditional models of exposure therapy involve the use of habituation—through repeated exposure—to quell anxiety. Modern exposure therapy takes habituation and adds inhibitory learning, which helps patients rewrite their memory or beliefs about their objects of fear. Rather than completely deleting their fears, patients learn to tamp them down. For instance, if a person has a snake phobia, therapy can teach them that with very rare exceptions, they will likely never encounter a dangerous snake.
paras.zh: 传统的暴露疗法模型涉及通过反复暴露来形成习惯来平息焦虑。现代暴露疗法需要习惯并增加抑制性学习，这有助于患者重写他们对恐惧对象的记忆或信念。患者并没有完全消除恐惧，而是学会压制恐惧。例如，如果一个人有蛇恐惧症，治疗可以告诉他们，除了极少数例外，他们可能永远不会遇到危险的蛇。

paras.en: “If you’re struggling with thoughts that are overwhelming, or if you’ve tried small exposures and your anxiety flares up, you may want to seek therapy,” Jerud says.
paras.zh: 杰鲁德说：“如果你正在与难以承受的想法作斗争，或者如果你尝试过少量的接触，但你的焦虑加剧，你可能需要寻求治疗。”

paras.en: Small, progressive exposures to the people, places, activities or memories that cause anxiety, conducted in a safe, controlled environment, can offer strategies to taming these aversions. In the clinic, a licensed therapist might guide a veteran with post-traumatic stress disorder through imagined exposure or someone afraid of spiders through real exposure—by gradually bringing them physically closer to the arachnids, for example—until they learn they are safe.
paras.zh: 在安全、受控的环境中进行小规模、渐进的接触引起焦虑的人、地方、活动或记忆，可以提供抑制这些厌恶的策略。在诊所里，有执照的治疗师可能会通过想象的暴露来指导患有创伤后应激障碍的退伍军人，或者通过真实的接触来引导害怕蜘蛛的人——例如，逐渐让他们在身体上更接近蜘蛛——直到他们知道自己是安全的。

paras.en: Therapist-led exposure therapy typically requires 15 to 20 sessions, according to Jerud, but every case is different. Patients need to do the “homework” that their therapist prescribes between sessions. “It’s like learning a new language,” Jerud says. “You need to practice outside of your appointments.”
paras.zh: Jerud 表示，治疗师主导的暴露疗法通常需要 15 到 20 次疗程，但每个案例都不同。患者需要在治疗期间完成治疗师规定的“作业”。 “这就像学习一门新语言，”杰鲁德说。 “你需要在预约之外练习。”

paras.en: A single exposure is unlikely to be enough—and as with learning a language, Conrad and Jerud recommend that individuals have “booster sessions” if anxiety flares up.
paras.zh: 一次接触不太可能足够——就像学习语言一样，康拉德和杰鲁德建议个人在焦虑发作时进行“加强课程”。

paras.en: As MacKenzie has learned on his own, exposure doesn’t eliminate your fear. But it does allow you to skillfully manage it. “Enough time on slides has served as positive reinforcement that I will be okay,” MacKenzie says.
paras.zh: 正如麦肯齐自己所了解到的那样，暴露并不能消除你的恐惧。但它确实可以让你熟练地管理它。 “足够的时间在幻灯片上已经起到了积极的作用，我会没事的，”麦肯齐说。

articles.title: AI could turn scientific papers into research assistants
articles.author: Kathryn Hulick

paras.en: Scientific papers may be getting a 21st century update.
paras.zh: 科学论文可能会在 21 世纪得到更新。

paras.en: A system called Paper2Agent lets scientists do more than read a new scientific study. When a paper comes with code, methods and data, the system packages these into a tool set that an AI assistant can use to work with new data, researchers report September 16 in Nature.
paras.zh: 一个名为 Paper2Agent 的系统可以让科学家做的不仅仅是阅读新的科学研究。研究人员于 9 月 16 日在《自然》杂志上报道，当一篇论文附带代码、方法和数据时，系统会将它们打包到一个工具集中，人工智能助手可以使用该工具集来处理新数据。

paras.en: The system is essentially “a virtual author of the paper,” available around the clock, says James Zou, a computer scientist at Stanford University.
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学计算机科学家 James Zou 表示，该系统本质上是“论文的虚拟作者”，全天候可用。

paras.en: In tests, Zou and colleagues tried to convert 100 computational biology papers into working tool sets and succeeded with 74. The others had obstacles such as missing code or data, or software that wouldn’t run. With the papers that were converted, the Paper2Agent tool set could run analyses of the published work and answer questions about the results. It did so more accurately and also more than twice as fast as the same agent working from the original papers and accompanying code.
paras.zh: 在测试中，Zou 和同事尝试将 100 篇计算生物学论文转换为工作工具集，其中 74 篇成功。其他论文则遇到了一些障碍，例如缺少代码或数据，或者软件无法运行。通过转换后的论文，Paper2Agent 工具集可以对已发表的论文进行分析并回答有关结果的问题。与使用原始论文和随附代码进行工作的同一代理相比，它的准确性更高，速度也快两倍多。

paras.en: Making another scientist’s code usable can take substantial work, says Peter Clark, a senior research director at the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Seattle who was not involved in developing Paper2Agent. Researchers already share code on platforms such as GitHub. But Clark says he often has to “grub around” for half a day to figure out how to get it running.
paras.zh: 西雅图艾伦人工智能研究所的高级研究主任彼得·克拉克（Peter Clark）没有参与 Paper2Agent 的开发，他表示，让另一位科学家的代码可用可能需要大量工作。研究人员已经在 GitHub 等平台上共享代码。但克拉克表示，他经常需要“摸索”半天才能弄清楚如何让它运行。

paras.en: A general-purpose AI assistant such as Claude can help, he says, but it typically generates new code on the fly. Paper2Agent instead packages code associated with a paper into reusable tools, tests them against reference outputs and writes step-by-step instructions guiding an AI assistant on which tools to use and in what order. This streamlines and standardizes the process of using AI to interact with scientific research, Clark says. It’s “an exciting step” toward papers that actively help scientists.
paras.zh: 他说，像克劳德这样的通用人工智能助手可以提供帮助，但它通常会动态生成新代码。 Paper2Agent 相反，将与论文相关的代码打包到可重用的工具中，根据参考输出对其进行测试，并编写分步指令，指导人工智能助手使用哪些工具以及按什么顺序使用。克拉克说，这简化并标准化了使用人工智能与科学研究互动的过程。这是朝着积极帮助科学家的论文迈出的“令人兴奋的一步”。

paras.en: To Zou, transforming scientific papers into agents seem like a natural next step for transmitting knowledge. We’ve already moved from stone tablets and papyrus to paper and then to digital formats, he says, and now it’s time to move from passive to active formats for human knowledge. A paper-agent can help one human scientist quickly use another’s code and methods. The tool can also search for paper-agents about similar topics with the aim of alerting their human authors about potential collaborations.
paras.zh: 对于邹来说，将科学论文转化为媒介似乎是传播知识的自然下一步。他说，我们已经从石碑和纸莎草纸转向纸张，然后转向数字格式，现在是人类知识从被动格式转向主动格式的时候了。论文代理可以帮助一位人类科学家快速使用另一位科学家的代码和方法。该工具还可以搜索类似主题的论文代理，目的是提醒人类作者潜在的合作。

paras.en: Zou says his team has already created “over 100 different paper-agents” from their own work and that these have already helped him find other scientists to collaborate with.
paras.zh: Zou 表示，他的团队已经根据自己的工作创建了“100 多种不同的纸质代理”，这些已经帮助他找到了其他科学家进行合作。

paras.en: Clark notes that Paper2Agent specializes in helping scientists reuse methods and code, and not in answering general questions, like a true virtual author should be able to do. Also, he worries about what could happen if millions of low-quality papers get turned into agents capable of pestering scientists. That could make things “worse rather than better,” he says, recalling the days of Clippy, the much-maligned Microsoft Office assistant. But he’d love for a “non-annoying agent” to pop up and tell him about work that he should be paying attention to.
paras.zh: Clark 指出，Paper2Agent 专门帮助科学家重用方法和代码，而不是像真正的虚拟作者那样回答一般问题。此外，他还担心，如果数以百万计的低质量论文变成了能够困扰科学家的媒介，会发生什么。他回忆起饱受诟病的 Microsoft Office 助手 Clippy 的日子时说，这可能会让事情“变得更糟而不是更好”。但他希望有一个“不烦人的代理人”突然出现并告诉他他应该关注的工作。

paras.en: For more open-ended questions about a paper, Clark says he would still want to talk to the people who did the research. “The reason I would write to a corresponding author is for precisely the things they didn’t put in the paper.”
paras.zh: 对于有关论文的更多开放式问题，克拉克表示他仍然想与进行这项研究的人交谈。 “我之所以给通讯作者写信，正是因为他们没有在论文中提到的内容。”

articles.title: Electric stoves could help people with asthma breathe easier
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: For people with asthma, switching from a gas stove to an electric one might be a breath of fresh air. The combustion that creates the flame of a gas stove or oven releases pollutants, including nitrogen dioxide, which can trigger asthma symptoms. After a research-backed electric stove replacement, people reported more symptom relief than is often achieved with asthma medications.
paras.zh: 对于患有哮喘的人来说，从煤气炉换成电炉可能是呼吸新鲜空气。燃气灶或烤箱燃烧产生的火焰会释放污染物，包括二氧化氮，这可能引发哮喘症状。在研究支持的电炉更换后，人们报告症状缓解效果比使用哮喘药物更明显。

paras.en: “We were really surprised at how large the benefit was,” says Ashwini Sehgal, a clinician who studies community health at Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland. With funding from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency during the Biden administration, Sehgal and colleagues spearheaded a project to install electric stoves in Cleveland households that had at least one person with asthma.
paras.zh: “我们对效果之大感到非常惊讶，”克利夫兰凯斯西储大学研究社区健康的临床医生阿什维尼·塞加尔 (Ashwini Sehgal) 说。在拜登执政期间，在美国环境保护署的资助下，塞加尔和同事牵头了一个项目，为克利夫兰至少有一名哮喘患者的家庭安装电炉。

paras.en: Eighty-five participants who had poorly controlled asthma were given a questionnaire a few months after the switch. They reported symptom improvement that was roughly two to three times as large as what’s typical with medication. Those with the worst symptoms saw the biggest improvement. Participants also reported fewer emergency room or hospital visits and said they missed work or school less often.
paras.zh: 转换后几个月，对 85 名哮喘控制不佳的参与者进行了问卷调查。他们报告说，症状改善程度大约是典型药物治疗的两到三倍。那些症状最严重的人看到了最大的改善。参与者还表示，去急诊室或医院的次数减少了，并且缺勤或缺课的次数也减少了。

paras.en: One 38-year-old woman told Sehgal’s team that whenever she cooked on her gas stove, she felt like her throat was closing. But the sensation disappeared after she switched to electric. Another participant, a 36-year-old man, found it difficult to walk uphill and play with his kids. With the stove swap, “he described how much better he felt as ‘magical,’ ” Sehgal says.
paras.zh: 一位 38 岁的女性告诉 Sehgal 的团队，每当她在煤气炉上做饭时，她都会感觉喉咙发紧。但当她改用电动后，这种感觉就消失了。另一位参与者是一名 36 岁的男子，他发现很难步行上山并与孩子们玩耍。更换炉灶后，“他形容自己感觉‘神奇’了很多，”塞加尔说。

paras.en: While heating, steaming or frying on a gas stovetop, nearby NO2 levels can skyrocket, reaching hundreds of parts per billion. That’s much higher than the EPA’s one-hour outdoor air quality standard of 100 parts per billion. NO2 exposure is linked to increased asthma symptoms. For example, research in children has found the pollutant can boost wheezing, coughing and asthma attacks.
paras.zh: 在燃气灶上加热、蒸或煎炸时，附近的二氧化氮浓度会飙升，达到十亿分之数百。这远高于 EPA 规定的一小时室外空气质量标准（十亿分之一百）。 NO2 暴露与哮喘症状加重有关。例如，针对儿童的研究发现污染物会加剧喘息、咳嗽和哮喘发作。

paras.en: The project was initially funded to follow 1,200 households for 12 months. But the Trump administration terminated the EPA’s Community Change Grants early, which drastically reduced the number of study participants. Yet even with this small group, the symptom improvement was significant.
paras.zh: 该项目最初的资助是对 1,200 个家庭进行为期 12 个月的跟踪。但特朗普政府提前终止了美国环保局的社区变革拨款，这大大减少了研究参与者的数量。然而，即使对于这一小群人来说，症状的改善也是显着的。

paras.en: The decision to replace a gas stove “depends on how much you are struggling with your own illness,” says environmental epidemiologist Carrie Breton of WashU Bursky School of Public Health in St. Louis. As a trial run, Sehgal suggests using an electric hot plate and a toaster oven to see if keeping the gas stove off helps improve symptoms.
paras.zh: 圣路易斯华盛顿大学伯斯基公共卫生学院的环境流行病学家卡丽·布雷顿（Carrie Breton）表示，更换燃气灶的决定“取决于你与自己的疾病作斗争的程度”。作为试运行，塞加尔建议使用电热板和烤面包机烤箱，看看关闭燃气灶是否有助于改善症状。

paras.en: If a stove swap isn’t in the budget, reducing NO2 exposure is still worthwhile, says pulmonologist Laura Paulin of Dartmouth Health. She recommends using kitchen ventilation, either via an exhaust hood that vents to the outside or an open window. A HEPA filter with a carbon insert can trap NO2 to decrease airborne concentrations. And try to keep children with asthma out of the kitchen when the stove is on, Paulin says. “It is a daunting task to replace a stove, but it doesn’t have to be an all-or-nothing thing.”
paras.zh: 达特茅斯健康中心的肺病学家劳拉·保林表示，如果预算中没有更换炉灶，减少二氧化氮暴露仍然是值得的。她建议使用厨房通风，可以通过通向室外的排气罩或打开的窗户。带有碳插件的 HEPA 过滤器可以捕获二氧化氮，以降低空气中的浓度。波林说，当炉子打开时，尽量让患有哮喘的孩子远离厨房。 “更换炉子是一项艰巨的任务，但不一定是全有或全无的事情。”

paras.en: For researchers, the next step would be to measure lung function before and after a stove switch, Breton says. It would also be helpful to account for more factors, such as seasonal effects. “Many things can trigger people’s asthma,” Paulin says. Researchers could do a randomized trial in which some people get the electric stove right away while others wait for six months, Sehgal says, to allow time for comparison.
paras.zh: 布雷顿说，对于研究人员来说，下一步将是测量炉灶开关前后的肺功能。考虑更多因素（例如季节性影响）也会有所帮助。 “很多事情都会引发人们的哮喘，”保林说。塞加尔说，研究人员可以进行一项随机试验，其中一些人立即使用电炉，而另一些人则等待六个月，以便有时间进行比较。

paras.en: If electric stoves continue to be linked with fewer trips to the emergency room, fewer hospitalizations and better symptom control than medication can provide, “health insurance companies should consider paying for or subsidizing” stove swaps, Sehgal says. “If it truly works this well,” Breton says, “it’s got a bigger bang for your buck.”
paras.zh: 塞加尔说，如果电炉继续与更少的急诊室次数、更少的住院次数和比药物更好的症状控制联系在一起，“健康保险公司应该考虑支付或补贴”炉灶更换。 “如果它真的运作得这么好，”布雷顿说，“那么你的钱就会得到更大的回报。”

articles.title: Eating too much sugar on antibiotics could squash helpful gut bacteria
articles.author: Mariella Careaga

paras.en: While a spoonful of sugar might help us gulp down a bitter-tasting antibiotic, it also may increase the damage that these drugs cause to the gut microbes.
paras.zh: 虽然一勺糖可能会帮助我们吞下苦味抗生素，但它也可能会增加这些药物对肠道微生物造成的损害。

paras.en: In patients being treated for blood cancers, eating sugary items during antibiotic treatment was linked to a greater reduction in gut bacteria diversity than taking the antibiotics alone. The combination was also tied to the growth of gut bacteria associated with hard-to-treat infections, researchers report September 30 in Nature.
paras.zh: 在接受血癌治疗的患者中，与单独服用抗生素相比，在抗生素治疗期间吃含糖食物会导致肠道细菌多样性更大程度的减少。研究人员于 9 月 30 日在《自然》杂志上报道称，这种组合还与肠道细菌的生长有关，这些细菌与难以治疗的感染有关。

paras.en: Cancer patients have lots of variation in their diets and take medications that can damage their microbiome. So, these patients provide a unique opportunity to study dramatic gut changes “that we believe are also relevant in the healthy context,” says Jonas Schluter, a microbiologist at NYU Langone Health.
paras.zh: 癌症患者的饮食有很大差异，并且服用的药物可能会损害他们的微生物群。因此，这些患者提供了一个独特的机会来研究肠道的巨大变化，“我们认为这些变化与健康环境相关，”纽约大学兰格尼健康中心的微生物学家乔纳斯·施卢特说。

paras.en: Previous evidence separately suggested that antibiotics and sugars can disrupt the gut microbiome. But their combined effects, particularly in people at greater risk of infection, was unclear.
paras.zh: 先前的证据分别表明抗生素和糖会破坏肠道微生物组。但它们的综合影响，特别是对感染风险较高的人来说，尚不清楚。

paras.en: Researchers closely tracked more than 9,000 meals eaten by 173 people hospitalized in a treatment center to undergo blood-forming stem cell transplants. “Diet records are one of the biggest black boxes in a lot of diet microbiome studies,” since meals are often self-reported, says Tiffany Weir, a microbiologist at Colorado State University in Fort Collins, who was not involved in the research.
paras.zh: 研究人员密切追踪了 173 名在治疗中心接受造血干细胞移植住院治疗的患者所吃的 9000 多顿饭。 “饮食记录是许多饮食微生物组研究中最大的黑匣子之一”，因为膳食通常是自我报告的，科林斯堡科罗拉多州立大学的微生物学家蒂芙尼·威尔（Tiffany Weir）说，她没有参与这项研究。

paras.en: Standardized hospital meals allowed researchers to measure multiple days’ worth of food intake down to the gram, then compare the amounts of various nutrients eaten with bacterial diversity data obtained from stool samples.
paras.zh: 标准化的医院膳食使研究人员能够测量多天的食物摄入量，精确到克，然后将摄入的各种营养素的量与从粪便样本中获得的细菌多样性数据进行比较。

paras.en: For every additional 100 grams of sugar (the equivalent of 2.5 cans of Coke) that patients on antibiotics ate in the two days before sampling, the team found a 24 percent decrease in bacterial diversity. Consuming sweets and sugary beverages during antibiotic treatment was also associated with blooms of Enterococcus bacteria, which can be drug-resistant and are linked to difficult-to-treat infections associated with longer hospital stays and higher mortality.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，服用抗生素的患者在采样前两天每多吃 100 克糖（相当于 2.5 罐可乐），细菌多样性就会减少 24%。在抗生素治疗期间食用甜食和含糖饮料也与肠球菌大量繁殖有关，肠球菌可能具有耐药性，并与难以治疗的感染有关，从而导致住院时间更长和死亡率更高。

paras.en: “Some bacteria, sometimes, survive antibiotics, or perhaps more dangerously, they are resistant to [them],” Schluter says. By giving these bacteria the “universal resource for life, which is simple sugars, we are exacerbating their dominance. It’s almost like burning down the rainforest with a lot of fire, and then trying to extinguish the flames by putting in more petrol.”
paras.zh: “有些细菌有时能够在抗生素的作用下存活下来，或者更危险的是，它们对抗生素产生抗药性，”施卢特说。通过为这些细菌提供“生命的通用资源，即单糖，我们正在加剧它们的统治地位。这几乎就像用大量的火烧毁雨林，然后试图通过加入更多的汽油来扑灭火焰。”

paras.en: The researchers also exposed mice on standard or sucrose-rich diets to a single dose of antibiotics. They found that the sugar exacerbated the enterococcal abundance after antibiotic exposure.
paras.zh: 研究人员还将标准饮食或富含蔗糖饮食的小鼠暴露于单剂量的抗生素。他们发现，接触抗生素后，糖会加剧肠球菌的丰度。

paras.en: “Reducing sugar intake could be another way for patients to support their gut microbiome during antibiotic treatment,” says Sarah Berry, a nutrition scientist at King’s College London who was not involved in the study. Still, more research is needed to determine whether the findings apply to anyone on these drugs.
paras.zh: “减少糖的摄入量可能是患者在抗生素治疗期间支持肠道微生物组的另一种方式，”伦敦国王学院的营养科学家莎拉·贝里（Sarah Berry）说，她没有参与这项研究。尽管如此，还需要更多的研究来确定这些发现是否适用于任何服用这些药物的人。

paras.en: Schluter hopes that further studies and clinical trials can help uncover more about the exact relationship between sugar, antibiotics and the gut microbiome.
paras.zh: 施卢特希望进一步的研究和临床试验能够帮助揭示更多关于糖、抗生素和肠道微生物组之间的确切关系。

paras.en: “You need to take antibiotics to fight infections, but you should also be aware that they have side effects to the microbiome,” Schluter says. “Now, we need to find strategies to mitigate this damage.”
paras.zh: “你需要服用抗生素来对抗感染，但你也应该意识到它们对微生物组有副作用，”施鲁特说。 “现在，我们需要找到减轻这种损害的策略。”

articles.title: We're a Step Closer to Quantum Computers That Can Correct Their Own Mistakes
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: Quantum computers promise an incredible leap forward in terms of performance, but a lot of that promise is still locked away as potential. The quantum computers we have today are relatively small-scale, limited prototypes of what might eventually be possible.
paras.zh: 量子计算机承诺在性能方面实现令人难以置信的飞跃，但其中很多承诺仍然被锁定为潜力。我们今天拥有的量子计算机规模相对较小，最终可能的原型也有限。

paras.en: One of the major challenges to scaling up and expanding quantum computer technology is the need to build in fault tolerance: being able to spot and fix errors at the same time as the computer is running through its calculations.
paras.zh: 扩大和扩展量子计算机技术的主要挑战之一是需要建立容错能力：能够在计算机运行计算的同时发现并修复错误。

paras.en: Now, researchers from the US have published a new study in Nature Physics that partly demonstrates how real-time error correction could work. The team set up a two-stage system designed to both introduce chaos and then correct for it, which is the same basic mechanism that's going to be needed for fault tolerance.
paras.zh: 现在，美国研究人员在《自然物理学》上发表了一项新研究，部分展示了实时纠错的工作原理。该团队建立了一个两阶段系统，旨在引入混乱，然后对其进行纠正，这与容错所需的基本机制相同。

paras.en: "To build a fault-tolerant quantum computer, we have to make these checks and corrections not just once or twice, but a huge number of times during a calculation," says physicist Jedediah Pixley, from Rutgers University in the US.
paras.zh: 美国罗格斯大学的物理学家杰迪戴亚·皮克斯利 (Jedediah Pixley) 表示：“为了构建一台容错量子计算机，我们必须在计算过程中进行多次检查和纠正，而不是一两次。”

paras.en: "This experiment is a landmark on that road. It says, okay, we've taken another important step to get there."
paras.zh: “这个实验是这条道路上的一个里程碑。它表明，好吧，我们为实现这一目标又迈出了重要的一步。”

paras.en: Classical computers run on bits, which are set as either 1 or 0. The qubits inside quantum computers can be 1, 0, or anywhere in between (existing in a superposition), until they're measured – and that's where the exponential upgrade in calculations comes from.
paras.zh: 经典计算机在位上运行，位设置为 1 或 0。量子计算机内的量子位可以是 1、0 或之间的任何位置（以叠加形式存在），直到它们被测量 - 这就是计算指数级升级的来源。

paras.en: Qubits are also incredibly delicate, and very susceptible to interference from environmental variables like heat or motion. That's why error correction is so important.
paras.zh: 量子位也非常脆弱，并且非常容易受到热或运动等环境变量的干扰。这就是为什么纠错如此重要。

paras.en: To test their new approach, the researchers used a 156-qubit IBM Quantum Heron processor, connecting together as many as 100 qubits at once. The system was then configured with two alternating tasks: scrambling (spreading chaos through the system), and controlling (resetting qubits where needed).
paras.zh: 为了测试他们的新方法，研究人员使用了 156 量子位 IBM Quantum Heron 处理器，一次将多达 100 个量子位连接在一起。然后，系统配置了两个交替的任务：加扰（在系统中传播混乱）和控制（在需要时重置量子位）。

paras.en: "The challenge was not simply to measure a qubit, but to do it repeatedly while the rest of the processor continued to operate," says physicist Maika Takita, from IBM.
paras.zh: IBM 物理学家 Maika Takita 表示：“挑战不仅仅是测量一个量子位，而是在处理器的其余部分继续运行的情况下重复测量。”

paras.en: "This experiment shows that present-day hardware can coordinate quantum operations, measurements and resets thousands of times across a large system."
paras.zh: “这项实验表明，当今的硬件可以在大型系统中协调量子操作、测量和重置数千次。”

paras.en: The researchers shifted the balance between scrambling and resetting during the course of their experiments. Across nearly 5,000 qubit operations and almost 5,000 checks and resets, order was resumed when the checks and resets made up more than half of the operations overall.
paras.zh: 研究人员在实验过程中改变了加扰和重置之间的平衡。在近 5,000 次量子位操作和近 5,000 次检查和重置中，当检查和重置占全部操作的一半以上时，秩序得以恢复。

paras.en: As more qubits were added, the tipping point became more well defined in the data – evidence that this is a true quantum effect and a phase transition, like water turning into ice in a unified way.
paras.zh: 随着更多量子位的添加，数据中的临界点变得更加明确——证据表明这是真正的量子效应和相变，就像水以统一的方式变成冰一样。

paras.en: "The agreement between the experiment and the theory showed that this was not an accidental feature of a small circuit. It was collective behavior emerging across the quantum system," says physicist Haining Pan, from the University of Florida.
paras.zh: “实验与理论之间的一致性表明，这不是小电路的偶然特征。这是整个量子系统中出现的集体行为，”佛罗里达大学的物理学家潘海宁说。

paras.en: Quantum computers won't become standard household gadgets like regular computers any time soon, but they will help in high-level, incredibly complex information processing tasks: testing drug development, forecasting the weather, simulating materials, powering AI, and much more.
paras.zh: 量子计算机不会很快成为像普通计算机一样的标准家用设备，但它们将有助于完成高级、极其复杂的信息处理任务：测试药物开发、预测天气、模拟材料、为人工智能提供动力等等。

paras.en: Now we know that the same mathematical checks and balances for chaos theory – the idea that the flap of a butterfly's wings in Brazil can ultimately set off a tornado in Texas – can work in a quantum as well as a classical setting.
paras.zh: 现在我们知道，混沌理论中相同的数学制衡——巴西蝴蝶翅膀的扇动最终可能在德克萨斯州引发龙卷风的想法——可以在量子和经典环境中发挥作用。

paras.en: The system of checking and resetting demonstrated here is going to need to be scaled up, using rules of greater complexity, to actually be of use in quantum computing – but it works as a stress test of feedback loops that can keep quantum systems running smoothly and in an ordered way.
paras.zh: 这里演示的检查和重置系统需要使用更复杂的规则进行扩展，才能真正用于量子计算——但它可以作为反馈循环的压力测试，可以保持量子系统平稳有序地运行。

paras.en: "Out-of-control behavior can be brought under control by randomly intervening, and there is a sharply defined rate at which that happens," says physicist Justin Wilson, from Louisiana State University.
paras.zh: 路易斯安那州立大学的物理学家贾斯汀·威尔逊说：“失控的行为可以通过随机干预来控制，而且这种情况发生的速度是有明确定义的。”

paras.en: "It wasn't obvious that this transition between chaos and control would survive in quantum physics, but our results show that it does."
paras.zh: “混沌与控制之间的这种转变是否会在量子物理学中继续存在并不明显，但我们的结果表明确实如此。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Physics.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然物理学》上。

articles.title: 16 Years After Deepwater Horizon Spill, Deep Sea Life in The Gulf of Mexico Shows No Sign of Recovery
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: In 2010, the Deepwater Horizon oil rig failed catastrophically, leading to the largest oil spill in the history of Earth's oceans.
paras.zh: 2010年，深水地平线石油钻井平台发生灾难性故障，导致地球海洋历史上最大规模的石油泄漏。

paras.en: About 134 million gallons of crude oil entered the Gulf of Mexico during the 87 days it took to cap the oil well, as well as 7.7 billion standard cubic feet of gas.
paras.zh: 在封堵油井的 87 天内，约有 1.34 亿加仑的原油以及 77 亿标准立方英尺的天然气进入墨西哥湾。

paras.en: Now, 16 years later, deep-sea ecosystems in the Gulf still show no sign of recovery from the disaster.
paras.zh: 16年后的今天，海湾深海生态系统仍然没有从灾难中恢复的迹象。

paras.en: Scientists from institutions in the US present these grim findings in a new paper published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: 来自美国机构的科学家在《美国国家科学院院刊》上发表的一篇新论文中介绍了这些严峻的发现。

paras.en: Led by oceanographer Tracey Sutton of Nova Southeastern University, the team focused on deep pelagic marine species, which are those that live deep in the water column.
paras.zh: 该团队由诺瓦东南大学的海洋学家特雷西·萨顿领导，重点研究深海海洋物种，即生活在水体深处的物种。

paras.en: They first collected net samples in 2011, right after the oil spill. When they returned in 2015 through to 2023, their samples (now more than 2,000 nets' worth, altogether) revealed a sharp crash in the abundance of deep pelagic species.
paras.zh: 他们于 2011 年漏油事件发生后首次收集了净样本。当他们在 2015 年至 2023 年返回时，他们的样本（现在总共超过 2,000 个净值）显示，深海中上层物种的丰度急剧下降。

paras.en: "We saw this big decline," Sutton told Seth Borenstein at Associated Press.
paras.zh: “我们看到了这种巨大的下降，”萨顿告诉美联社的塞斯博伦斯坦。

paras.en: "The question was then why? So we looked at all of the natural variables we thought could account for it, namely temperature, oxygen supply, and food. None of those vary with the decline. The event that did was the oil spill. So we think that's the most likely cause of the decline."
paras.zh: “问题是为什么？所以我们研究了我们认为可以解释的所有自然变量，即温度、氧气供应和食物。这些都不会随着下降而变化。造成这种下降的事件是石油泄漏。所以我们认为这是最有可能导致下降的原因。”

paras.en: Fish numbers were down 63.5 percent; crustaceans by 62 percent; and cephalopods (mainly squid, in this context) by 59.7 percent.
paras.zh: 鱼类数量下降 63.5%；甲壳类动物减少 62%；头足类动物（主要是鱿鱼）增加了 59.7%。

paras.en: "The taxa that declined the most are also considered the most ecologically important in the open ocean with respect to total numbers, biogeochemical cycling, and prey provisioning for higher trophic levels," the authors write.
paras.zh: 作者写道：“就总数、生物地球化学循环和更高营养水平的猎物供应而言，下降幅度最大的类群也被认为是公海中生态最重要的类群。”

paras.en: Those taxa include krill, which declined by 72.8 percent; lanternfishes, which declined by 62.9 percent; and Cyclothone bristlemouth fishes, which declined by 69 percent.
paras.zh: 这些类群包括磷虾，减少了 72.8%；灯笼鱼下降了62.9%；和 Cyclothone 鬃口鱼，减少了 69%。

paras.en: All of these animals are vital prey for the ecosystem, and fuel the fishing and tourism economies people have built around it.
paras.zh: 所有这些动物都是生态系统的重要猎物，并为人们围绕生态系统建立的渔业和旅游业经济提供了动力。

paras.en: Many of them belong to what is known as the 'deep scattering layer', which contains fish, squid, and other creatures that rise towards the surface at night, and return to the deep at dawn, traveling hundreds of vertical meters.
paras.zh: 其中许多属于所谓的“深层散射层”，其中包含鱼类、鱿鱼和其他生物，它们在夜间升到水面，并在黎明时返回深处，垂直移动数百米。

paras.en: This daily movement is like a 'biological pump' that drives carbon sequestration in the deep ocean.
paras.zh: 这种日常运动就像一个“生物泵”，推动深海碳封存。

paras.en: "The community of organisms that comprise the deep scattering layer is a diverse complex of animals," marine scientist Kevin Boswell says.
paras.zh: 海洋科学家凯文·博斯韦尔说：“构成深层散射层的生物群落是一个多样化的动物复合体。”

paras.en: "To be able to measure changes in the ecosystem across independent methodologies really drives home the point that the midwater ecosystem has undergone a significant change."
paras.zh: “能够通过独立的方法来衡量生态系统的变化，确实让我们明白了中层水域生态系统已经发生了重大变化。”

paras.en: The repercussions of such a drastic collapse in the deep scattering layer may be surfacing already. Some shipboard researchers have reported sightings of 'thin whales', while once-predictable sperm whales seem to be moving erratically around the Gulf in search of food.
paras.zh: 深层散射层中这种剧烈塌陷的影响可能已经浮现出来。一些船上研究人员报告称看到了“瘦鲸”，而曾经可预测的抹香鲸似乎正在海湾地区不稳定地移动以寻找食物。

paras.en: The researchers say the oil spill is the "most parsimonious explanation" for the drastic changes to the Gulf's deep sea ecosystem.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，漏油事件是海湾深海生态系统发生巨大变化的“最简单的解释”。

paras.en: "Available evidence rules out natural phenomena as likely drivers, suggesting a large-scale pollution event and its associated mitigation measures most likely precipitated the declines," the authors write.
paras.zh: 作者写道：“现有证据排除了自然现象可能是驱动因素的可能性，这表明大规模污染事件及其相关的缓解措施很可能导致了下降。”

paras.en: Those associated mitigation measures include around 770,000 gallons of the chemical dispersant Corexit 9500A that were injected near the wellhead.
paras.zh: 这些相关缓解措施包括在井口附近注入约 770,000 加仑化学分散剂 Corexit 9500A。

paras.en: The idea was to break up the oil and prevent massive oil slicks that could choke life on the Gulf's surface and shores, but this approach comes at a cost. The spill reached much farther than satellite images indicated, because oil residues reached all the way to the sea floor.
paras.zh: 这个想法是为了分解石油并防止大量浮油可能窒息海湾表面和海岸的生命，但这种方法是有代价的。泄漏的范围比卫星图像显示的要远得多，因为石油残留物一直到达海底。

paras.en: Both the oil and the dispersant are toxic to marine life, particularly the zooplankton that form the foundation of marine food chains. Combined, they do even more damage to zooplankton than the oil does on its own.
paras.zh: 石油和分散剂对海洋生物有毒，特别是对构成海洋食物链基础的浮游动物。它们加起来对浮游动物造成的损害甚至比石油本身造成的损害还要大。

paras.en: In 2014, scientists predicted that "the negative impact of crude oil and dispersant on microzooplankton may disrupt the transfer of energy from lower to higher trophic levels and change the structure and dynamics of marine planktonic communities."
paras.zh: 2014年，科学家预测“原油和分散剂对微型浮游动物的负面影响可能会破坏能量从较低营养级到较高营养级的转移，并改变海洋浮游生物群落的结构和动态。”

paras.en: The new research potentially shows those outcomes in action.
paras.zh: 这项新研究可能会展示这些结果的实际作用。

paras.en: "Our findings are particularly concerning because these are species that are abundant, widespread, and historically might not have been considered vulnerable," says marine biologist Pedro Peres of Florida International University.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达国际大学的海洋生物学家佩德罗·佩雷斯说：“我们的发现尤其令人担忧，因为这些物种数量丰富、分布广泛，而且历史上可能不会被认为是脆弱的。”

paras.en: "Even species that appear abundant can experience substantial changes that may go unnoticed without monitoring."
paras.zh: “即使是看起来丰富的物种也可能经历重大变化，如果不进行监测，这些变化可能会被忽视。”

paras.en: "Collectively, these results indicate a sudden and persistent decline in the deep-pelagic fauna of a large marine ecosystem, resulting in a sustained, low-abundance state that meets the criteria for an ecological regime shift," the authors write.
paras.zh: 作者写道：“总的来说，这些结果表明大型海​​洋生态系统的深海动物群突然持续减少，导致持续的低丰度状态，符合生态状况转变的标准。”

paras.en: They are unsure if recovery will ever be possible, let alone how long it would take.
paras.zh: 他们不确定是否能够恢复，更不用说需要多长时间了。

paras.en: "Given the tightly connected nature of oceanic life in the Gulf specifically… such declines are likely to reverberate through the system from top to bottom, altering ecosystem functions across multiple levels," they conclude.
paras.zh: 他们总结道：“特别是考虑到海湾地区海洋生物紧密相连的性质……这种下降可能会从上到下影响整个系统，在多个层面上改变生态系统功能。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

articles.title: Researchers Developed a Molecule to Fight Alzheimer's – Then Found It's Already in Our Blood
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: A significant amount of Alzheimer's research is looking at ways to tackle the harmful clumps of amyloid-beta protein that build up between neurons in the brains of people with the disease.
paras.zh: 阿尔茨海默病的大量研究正在寻找方法来解决阿尔茨海默病患者大脑神经元之间形成的有害的β-淀粉样蛋白团块。

paras.en: With that same aim, researchers from the startup Lifemission and the Russian Academy of Sciences previously developed a peptide called HAEE (Ac-His-Ala-Glu-Glu-NH2) to stop these clumps from forming by blocking zinc ions that are thought to act as a kind of biological 'glue'.
paras.zh: 出于同样的目标，初创公司 Lifemission 和俄罗斯科学院的研究人员此前开发了一种名为 HAEE（Ac-His-Ala-Glu-Glu-NH2）的肽，通过阻止锌离子来阻止这些团块的形成，锌离子被认为是一种生物“粘合剂”。

paras.en: In tests on mice, the peptide has already been shown to reduce the number of amyloid-beta plaques in the brain.
paras.zh: 在对小鼠的测试中，该肽已被证明可以减少大脑中淀粉样蛋白斑块的数量。

paras.en: Now there's a plot twist: When the researchers developed a method to measure HAEE in human blood as a step toward clinical trials, they found the peptide was already present – in every sample from 150 healthy volunteers.
paras.zh: 现在出现了一个转折：当研究人员开发出一种测量人体血液中 HAEE 的方法作为临床试验的一步时，他们发现这种肽已经存在于 150 名健康志愿者的每个样本中。

paras.en: What's more, the blood samples taken from people with Alzheimer's had around half the level of HAEE on average as healthy controls, suggesting the molecule could even be used as a disease biomarker. The findings have been published in PNAS Nexus.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，从阿尔茨海默氏症患者身上采集的血液样本中，HAEE 水平平均约为健康对照者的一半，这表明该分子甚至可以用作疾病生物标志物。研究结果发表在 PNAS Nexus 上。

paras.en: "We discovered that the human blood contains an endogenous replica of this peptide, and that its concentration is sharply reduced in patients with a clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“我们发现人类血液中含有这种肽的内源性复制品，并且在临床诊断为阿尔茨海默病的患者中，其浓度急剧降低。”

paras.en: "Our findings uncover a new molecule of the human body and suggest that endogenous HAEE deficiency plays a significant role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease."
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果揭示了人体的一种新分子，并表明内源性 HAEE 缺陷在阿尔茨海默病的发病机制中发挥着重要作用。”

paras.en: Before a drug can be tested in a clinical trial, scientists need to know how it breaks down in the blood over time, and what level of dosage is going to be safe – which is the original reasoning behind the blood tests.
paras.zh: 在临床试验中测试一种药物之前，科学家需要知道它随着时间的推移如何在血液中分解，以及什么剂量水平才是安全的——这是血液测试背后的最初推理。

paras.en: It's a discovery that seems to back up the research team's thinking that HAEE can be an important influence on the development of Alzheimer's. However, working out the exact relationship and its mechanisms is going to need further study.
paras.zh: 这一发现似乎支持了研究小组的想法，即 HAEE 可能对阿尔茨海默氏症的发展产生重要影响。然而，弄清楚确切的关系及其机制还需要进一步研究。

paras.en: "The HAEE deficiency in the blood of patients clinically diagnosed with AAlzheimer's disease compared to healthy volunteers shown in the present study may be caused by suppression of normal HAEE generation and/or excessive HAEE consumption due to the body's response to various types of stress associated with the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease," write the study authors.
paras.zh: 研究作者写道：“本研究显示，与健康志愿者相比，临床诊断为阿尔茨海默氏病的患者血液中 HAEE 缺乏可能是由于正常的 HAEE 生成受到抑制和/或由于身体对与阿尔茨海默氏病发病机制相关的各种压力的反应而导致 HAEE 消耗过多。”

paras.en: It could be that Alzheimer's means the body produces less HAEE, or that it gets used up faster as the disease takes hold, but right now the researchers aren't sure.
paras.zh: 阿尔茨海默病可能意味着身体产生的 HAEE 减少，或者随着疾病的发展，HAEE 消耗得更快，但目前研究人员还不确定。

paras.en: We know that amyloid-beta plaques tend to show up early in Alzheimer's disease, sometimes years before other symptoms appear, which strengthens the case for HAEE being used as a warning sign for the condition if it can be developed further – though this study only looked at people already diagnosed.
paras.zh: 我们知道，β-淀粉样蛋白斑块往往在阿尔茨海默病早期出现，有时比其他症状出现早几年，这加强了 HAEE 被用作该病进一步发展的警告信号的理由——尽管这项研究只关注已经诊断的人。

paras.en: "Deficiency of endogenous HAEE may be considered as a potential blood-based biomarker in the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, while exogenous synthetic HAEE may serve as a drug in Alzheimer's disease-modifying therapy," writes the team.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“内源性 HAEE 的缺乏可能被认为是诊断阿尔茨海默病的潜在血液生物标志物，而外源性合成 HAEE 可能作为阿尔茨海默病缓解疗法的药物。”

paras.en: The researchers acknowledge some limitations to their findings. Alzheimer's diagnoses were based on clinical assessments alone, without brain imaging or biomarker tests, so some patients may have had other forms of dementia.
paras.zh: 研究人员承认他们的研究结果存在一些局限性。阿尔茨海默氏症的诊断仅基于临床评估，没有脑成像或生物标志物测试，因此一些患者可能患有其他形式的痴呆症。

paras.en: There were also some variations in age between the Alzheimer's patients and the healthy controls, which may have contributed to the results, and HAEE levels didn't vary significantly by Alzheimer's severity.
paras.zh: 阿尔茨海默病患者和健康对照者之间的年龄也存在一些差异，这可能对结果有影响，而且 HAEE 水平不会因阿尔茨海默病的严重程度而发生显着变化。

paras.en: It's worth noting too that the study was funded by the startup Lifemission, which holds patents relating to HAEE as an Alzheimer's blood test. Two of the study researchers are also connected to the company.
paras.zh: 还值得注意的是，这项研究是由初创公司 Lifemission 资助的，该公司拥有与 HAEE 作为阿尔茨海默病血液测试相关的专利。其中两名研究人员也与该公司有联系。

paras.en: Even with those caveats, it's a significant new finding in the study of Alzheimer's and the work going on toward a cure. We know that it's a complex disease with many different facets, and HAEE may end up being an important one.
paras.zh: 即使有这些警告，这仍然是阿尔茨海默病研究和治疗工作中的一个重大新发现。我们知道这是一种复杂的疾病，具有许多不同的方面，而 HAEE 最终可能成为一个重要的疾病。

paras.en: "The discovery that a previously created peptide aimed at reducing amyloid burden in Alzheimer's disease has its endogenous replica in human blood plasma is remarkable," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“先前创建的一种旨在减少阿尔茨海默病中淀粉样蛋白负担的肽在人血浆中具有内源性复制品，这一发现是引人注目的。”

paras.en: "However, equally significant is the fact that levels of this peptide are reduced in patients with Alzheimer's disease."
paras.zh: “然而，同样重要的是，这种肽的水平在阿尔茨海默病患者中降低了。”

paras.en: The research has been published in PNAS Nexus.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在 PNAS Nexus 上。

articles.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial

paras.en: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
paras.zh: 突破性 PTSD 治疗在临床试验中达到 68% 的缓解率

paras.en: - A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.
paras.zh: - FDA 新批准的 PTSD 治疗方法使用个性化大脑绘图和磁刺激来针对异常的大脑活动，临床试验报告症状减少了 52%，症状缓解了 68%。研究人员相信，这项技术可以改变创伤后应激障碍 (PTSD) 护理，并为更精确地治疗其他心理健康状况铺平道路。

paras.en: A new approach to treating post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) has received FDA clearance, offering a personalized alternative for people who have not found sufficient relief through existing treatments. Developed by California-based Wave Neuroscience in collaboration with researchers at the Texas A&M Health Institute of Biosciences and Technology, the technology uses brain activity measurements to guide targeted magnetic stimulation.
paras.zh: 一种治疗创伤后应激障碍 (PTSD) 的新方法已获得 FDA 批准，为那些通过现有治疗尚未得到充分缓解的人们提供了个性化的替代方案。该技术由加利福尼亚州的 Wave Neuroscience 与德克萨斯 A&M 健康生物科学与技术研究所的研究人员合作开发，利用大脑活动测量来指导有针对性的磁刺激。

paras.en: Early clinical trial findings have been encouraging. According to Wave Neuroscience, patients experienced a 52% reduction in PTSD symptoms, while 68% achieved remission. The full findings are still being prepared for public release, but researchers believe the technology could significantly expand treatment options for millions of people.
paras.zh: 早期的临床试验结果令人鼓舞。根据 Wave Neuroscience 的数据，患者的 PTSD 症状减少了 52%，而 68% 的患者获得了缓解。完整的研究结果仍在准备公开发布，但研究人员相信该技术可以显着扩大数百万人的治疗选择。

paras.en: The need for more effective PTSD care is substantial. In the United States, approximately 17.5 veterans die by suicide each day, and about 7% of veterans receive a PTSD diagnosis annually.
paras.zh: 对更有效的创伤后应激障碍护理的需求是巨大的。在美国，每天约有 17.5 名退伍军人自杀身亡，每年约有 7% 的退伍军人被诊断为 PTSD。

paras.en: PTSD can develop after traumatic experiences such as military combat, serious accidents, natural disasters, or violence. An estimated 6% of Americans will experience PTSD during their lifetime, with higher rates among women and veterans.
paras.zh: 创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）可能在军事战斗、严重事故、自然灾害或暴力等创伤经历后发展。据估计，6% 的美国人在一生中会经历创伤后应激障碍 (PTSD)，其中女性和退伍军人的比例更高。

paras.en: Why Current PTSD Treatments Are Not Enough
paras.zh: 为什么目前的创伤后应激障碍治疗还不够

paras.en: Since PTSD was formally recognized as a diagnosis in 1980, treatment has largely centered on psychotherapy and medications known as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), including sertraline and fluoxetine.
paras.zh: 自 1980 年 PTSD 被正式认定为一种诊断以来，治疗主要集中在心理治疗和选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂 (SSRI) 药物，包括舍曲林和氟西汀。

paras.en: Although these approaches can help, many patients continue to experience symptoms despite receiving treatment.
paras.zh: 尽管这些方法可以有所帮助，但许多患者尽管接受治疗，但仍然出现症状。

paras.en: A 2020 review of PTSD medications found that patients reported improvements ranging from 6.8 to 10.1 points on symptom assessments. However, remission rates reached only 10.9% at most.
paras.zh: 2020 年对 PTSD 药物的审查发现，患者的症状评估改善了 6.8 到 10.1 分。然而，缓解率最多仅达到10.9%。

paras.en: Wave Neuroscience reported substantially stronger preliminary outcomes in its clinical trial. Erik Won, DO, the company's chief medical officer, described the results as a major advance over previously reported medication outcomes.
paras.zh: Wave Neuroscience 在其临床试验中报告了明显更强的初步结果。该公司首席医疗官 Erik Won（DO）将这一结果描述为比之前报道的药物治疗结果的重大进步。

paras.en: “In comparison to that study, our FDA trial reported a 52% reduction in symptoms, so more than a four-fold increase in efficacy,” Won said. “And more importantly, we saw 68% remission in our clinical trial. So, it’s really a quantum change, an inflection point in what we can offer to patients. From a clinical care perspective, that’s really meaningful.”
paras.zh: “与那项研究相比，我们的 FDA 试验报告症状减少了 52%，因此疗效提高了四倍多，”Won 说。 “更重要的是，我们在临床试验中看到了 68% 的缓解。因此，这确实是一个量子变化，是我们可以为患者提供的服务的转折点。从临床护理的角度来看，这非常有意义。”

paras.en: These findings are promising, although the results come from different studies and should not be interpreted as a direct comparison of treatment effectiveness.
paras.zh: 这些发现是有希望的，尽管结果来自不同的研究，不应被解释为治疗效果的直接比较。

paras.en: How Personalized Brain Stimulation Works
paras.zh: 个性化大脑刺激的工作原理

paras.en: The newly cleared system uses Magnetic e-Resonance Therapy (MeRT), a technology that combines measurements of brain activity with targeted magnetic stimulation.
paras.zh: 新批准的系统使用磁电子共振疗法（MeRT），这是一种将大脑活动测量与有针对性的磁刺激相结合的技术。

paras.en: First, an electroencephalogram (EEG) records the brain's electrical signals. This information helps guide a personalized treatment plan using transcranial magnetic stimulation, or TMS.
paras.zh: 首先，脑电图（EEG）记录大脑的电信号。这些信息有助于指导使用经颅磁刺激 (TMS) 的个性化治疗计划。

paras.en: During TMS, a coil positioned against the scalp delivers magnetic pulses that stimulate brain activity. The technique has already been used for other psychiatric conditions, including treatment-resistant depression.
paras.zh: 在 TMS 过程中，靠在头皮上的线圈会发出磁脉冲，刺激大脑活动。该技术已经用于其他精神疾病，包括难治性抑郁症。

paras.en: What distinguishes MeRT is its use of an AI-assisted algorithm to customize stimulation protocols based on each patient's brain activity rather than relying on a standardized approach.
paras.zh: MeRT 的独特之处在于它使用人工智能辅助算法根据每个患者的大脑活动定制刺激方案，而不是依赖标准化方法。

paras.en: “Transcranial magnetic stimulation, or TMS, was previously FDA cleared for treatment-resistant depression,” Won said. “By adding an augmented AI derived multivariate algorithm, we were able to personalize protocols that received FDA clearance for post-traumatic stress disorder, which should open up market access to about 13 million people who may be struggling with PTSD.”
paras.zh: “经颅磁刺激（TMS）此前已被 FDA 批准用于治疗难治性抑郁症，”Won 说。 “通过添加增强型人工智能衍生的多变量算法，我们能够个性化获得 FDA 批准的创伤后应激障碍治疗方案，这将为大约 1300 万可能患有 PTSD 的人打开市场准入。”

paras.en: Dr. Kenneth S. Ramos, a physician-scientist at Texas A&M Health with extensive experience in precision medicine, helped guide the research.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯 A&M 健康中心的医师科学家 Kenneth S. Ramos 博士在精准医学方面拥有丰富的经验，他帮助指导了这项研究。

paras.en: His work focuses on adapting medical care to the characteristics of individual patients instead of assuming that everyone will respond to the same treatment.
paras.zh: 他的工作重点是使医疗护理适应个体患者的特点，而不是假设每个人都会对相同的治疗产生反应。

paras.en: “Most clinical interventions for the treatment of PTSD do not work very well,” Ramos said. “So, this is a huge area where identifying interventions that could hopefully add quality of life to the people impacted by this disorder would be tremendously impactful.”
paras.zh: “大多数治疗创伤后应激障碍的临床干预措施效果不佳，”拉莫斯说。 “因此，这是一个巨大的领域，确定有望提高受这种疾病影响的人们的生活质量的干预措施将产生巨大的影响。”

paras.en: Wave Neuroscience CEO Fred Walke said Ramos was a natural fit for the project because of his expertise in personalized medicine.
paras.zh: Wave Neuroscience 首席执行官 Fred Walke 表示，Ramos 非常适合该项目，因为他在个性化医疗方面拥有专业知识。

paras.en: Conventional TMS generally follows treatment protocols that are less individualized. MeRT builds on the same underlying technology but adjusts treatment according to the patient's specific brain activity.
paras.zh: 传统的 TMS 通常遵循个性化程度较低的治疗方案。 MeRT 基于相同的基础技术，但根据患者的特定大脑活动调整治疗。

paras.en: Ramos emphasized that even small biological differences between people can have major implications for medical care. Humans are approximately 99.9% genetically alike, yet the remaining 0.1% contributes to differences that can influence how individuals respond to treatment.
paras.zh: 拉莫斯强调，即使人与人之间很小的生物学差异也会对医疗保健产生重大影响。人类大约 99.9% 的基因相似，但其余 0.1% 的差异会影响个体对治疗的反应。

paras.en: By accounting for these differences and tailoring stimulation to each person's brain, researchers observed substantial reductions in PTSD symptom severity.
paras.zh: 通过考虑这些差异并针对每个人的大脑定制刺激，研究人员观察到 PTSD 症状严重程度显着降低。

paras.en: Ramos illustrated the distinction with an analogy involving a leaking roof.
paras.zh: 拉莫斯用屋顶漏水的类比来说明这种区别。

paras.en: He likened conventional TMS to covering a leak with a tarp to manage its effects. MeRT, in contrast, aims to provide a more targeted solution, comparable to identifying and replacing the damaged shingles responsible for the problem.
paras.zh: 他将传统的 TMS 比作用防水布覆盖泄漏处以控制其影响。相比之下，MeRT 旨在提供更有针对性的解决方案，类似于识别和更换造成问题的受损木瓦。

paras.en: The broader goal is to move beyond treating patients with standardized protocols and toward interventions guided by measurable biological information.
paras.zh: 更广泛的目标是超越用标准化方案治疗患者，转向以可测量的生物信息为指导的干预措施。

paras.en: From Breakthrough Designation to FDA Clearance
paras.zh: 从突破性认定到 FDA 批准

paras.en: The regulatory process reached an important milestone in 2024, when MeRT received an FDA Breakthrough Device designation.
paras.zh: 2024 年，监管流程达到了一个重要的里程碑，MeRT 获得了 FDA 突破性器械称号。

paras.en: Dr. Rick Silva, executive director of clinical trials at the Texas A&M Health Institute of Biosciences and Technology, explained that the designation helps promising technologies move through regulatory review more efficiently.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯 A&M 健康生物科学与技术研究所临床试验执行主任 Rick Silva 博士解释说，这一称号有助于有前途的技术更有效地通过监管审查。

paras.en: It does not eliminate scientific or medical requirements. Instead, it can streamline communication and reduce administrative delays while preserving the standards needed for FDA clearance.
paras.zh: 它并没有消除科学或医学要求。相反，它可以简化沟通并减少行政延误，同时保留 FDA 审批所需的标准。

paras.en: Silva said the progress was particularly meaningful because the project began during the COVID-19 pandemic and advanced through the regulatory process unusually quickly.
paras.zh: Silva 表示，这一进展特别有意义，因为该项目是在 COVID-19 大流行期间启动的，并以异常快的速度通过了监管程序。

paras.en: According to Silva, medical device development and clinical evaluation can often take around 10 years before clearance is obtained. This project completed the relevant process in just over two years.
paras.zh: Silva 表示，医疗器械开发和临床评估通常需要 10 年左右才能获得许可。该项目仅用了两年多的时间就完成了相关流程。

paras.en: He credited the experience and dedication of the Wave Neuroscience team with helping make that accelerated progress possible.
paras.zh: 他称赞 Wave Neuroscience 团队的经验和奉献精神帮助加速了这一进展。

paras.en: “I’ve been involved in probably close to 1,000 projects in academic medical centers over the years at varying degrees of depth and detail,” Silva said. “Patients are why I do what I do. It’s hard, and the failure rate is high, and it’s a lot of work. But when you get to a point where something is going to benefit patients, it’s very professionally gratifying and personally gratifying in many ways as well.”
paras.zh: “多年来，我在学术医疗中心参与了大约近 1,000 个项目，深度和细节各不相同，”席尔瓦说。 “患者是我做这件事的原因。这很困难，失败率很高，而且工作量很大。但是当你的某件事能够使患者受益时，这在很多方面都是非常职业上的满足感和个人满足感。”

paras.en: A New Drug-Free Option for PTSD Patients
paras.zh: 创伤后应激障碍患者的新的无药选择

paras.en: Dr. Israel Liberzon, distinguished professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at the Texas A&M Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine, served as the study's lead psychiatrist and PTSD specialist.
paras.zh: Israel Liberzon 博士是德克萨斯 A&M Naresh K. Vashisht 医学院的精神病学和行为科学杰出教授，担任该研究的首席精神病学家和 PTSD 专家。

paras.en: He believes the clearance represents an important expansion of the available treatments for PTSD.
paras.zh: 他认为此次批准标志着创伤后应激障碍 (PTSD) 可用治疗方法的重要扩展。

paras.en: According to Liberzon, MeRT will become the only FDA-cleared nonmedication treatment specifically for PTSD once it reaches patients.
paras.zh: 据 Liberzon 称，一旦 MeRT 到达患者手中，它将成为 FDA 批准的唯一一种专门针对 PTSD 的非药物治疗方法。

paras.en: “Right now, the FDA has approved only two medications for PTSD,” Liberzon said. “It doesn’t mean that only two of them are used, but both are SSRIs. This is the first time that in addition to the medication, we have a non-medication option. There is psychotherapy that people use for PTSD, but psychotherapies require a lot of effort. People must participate actively, and many drop out because it’s too anxiety provoking. So now we have a unique alternative.”
paras.zh: “目前，FDA 只批准了两种治疗创伤后应激障碍的药物，”Liberzon 说。 “这并不意味着只使用其中两种，而是两者都是SSRI。这是我们第一次除了药物之外，还有非药物选择。人们有针对PTSD的心理治疗，但心理治疗需要付出很大的努力。人们必须积极参与，很多人因为太引起焦虑而退出。所以现在我们有一个独特的替代方案。”

paras.en: In the clinical trial, participants received five treatment sessions each week over a period of five to six weeks.
paras.zh: 在临床试验中，参与者在五到六周的时间内每周接受五次治疗。

paras.en: Researchers reported that the improvements appeared to persist after the treatment sessions ended, suggesting the benefits may extend beyond the active therapy period.
paras.zh: 研究人员报告说，治疗结束后，这种改善似乎仍然存在，这表明这种好处可能会延续到积极治疗期之后。

paras.en: For patients who struggle with medication side effects or find psychotherapy difficult to complete, a treatment based on personalized brain stimulation could provide another option.
paras.zh: 对于那些与药物副作用作斗争或发现心理治疗难以完成的患者来说，基于个性化大脑刺激的治疗可以提供另一种选择。

paras.en: “People living with PTSD have been left with trial-and-error treatment, medications and their side effects, and limited outcomes—even when treated by the most dedicated and experienced physicians,” Won said. “Wave’s FDA clearance signals a fundamentally different future: one in which PTSD can be objectively evaluated, precisely treated and meaningfully healed.”
paras.zh: “患有创伤后应激障碍的人只能接受反复试验的治疗、药物治疗及其副作用，而且即使由最敬业、经验丰富的医生治疗，结果也很有限，”Won 说。 “Wave 获得 FDA 批准标志着一个完全不同的未来：创伤后应激障碍 (PTSD) 可以得到客观评估、精确治疗和有意义的治愈。”

paras.en: Won also believes the technology could eventually be adapted to other psychiatric conditions, including depression and anxiety.
paras.zh: 元还相信，这项技术最终可以适应其他精神疾病，包括抑郁和焦虑。

paras.en: Could Personalized Brain Therapy Transform Mental Healthcare?
paras.zh: 个性化脑部治疗可以改变心理保健吗？

paras.en: Dr. Leslie S. Prichep, chief scientific officer at Wave Neuroscience, sees the FDA clearance as an important step toward treatment decisions guided by objective measurements of brain function.
paras.zh: Wave Neuroscience 首席科学官 Leslie S. Prichep 博士认为 FDA 的批准是朝着以脑功能客观测量为指导的治疗决策迈出的重要一步。

paras.en: “The FDA clearance of the MeRT System reflects decades of scientific research using electrophysiological biomarkers in identifying abnormal brain activity profiles and guiding personalized intervention strategies,” Prichep said. “We believe this represents an important advancement toward a more objective, data-informed model of mental healthcare.”
paras.zh: “FDA 对 MeRT 系统的批准反映了数十年来利用电生理生物标志物识别异常大脑活动特征并指导个性化干预策略的科学研究，”Prichep 说。 “我们相信，这代表着朝着更客观、以数据为依据的心理保健模式迈出了重要一步。”

paras.en: Walke believes that giving patients clearer information about their brain activity could also help change public attitudes toward mental illness.
paras.zh: 沃克认为，为患者提供有关其大脑活动的更清晰的信息也有助于改变公众对精神疾病的态度。

paras.en: He compared the idea to treating a broken bone with a cast. By making mental health conditions easier to understand through measurable physical information, the company hopes to reduce stigma and help patients better understand their experiences.
paras.zh: 他将这个想法比作用石膏治疗骨折。该公司希望通过可测量的身体信息让人们更容易了解心理健康状况，从而减少耻辱感并帮助患者更好地了解他们的经历。

paras.en: “One of the goals of the company is to create a platform for mental healthcare that uses objective imagery to help patients understand why they’re experiencing life the way that they are,” Walke said. “That insight, compounded with proven technologies, promises incredibly high efficacy when personalized.”
paras.zh: 沃克说：“公司的目标之一是创建一个心理保健平台，利用客观图像帮助患者理解为什么他们会经历现在的生活。” “这种洞察力与成熟的技术相结合，在个性化时保证了令人难以置信的高效率。”

paras.en: An important next step will be ensuring that patients can actually obtain the treatment. Wave Neuroscience and Texas A&M Health are working with other stakeholders to expand availability and make the therapy more affordable through insurance coverage.
paras.zh: 下一步重要的一步是确保患者能够真正获得治疗。 Wave Neuroscience 和 Texas A&M Health 正在与其他利益相关者合作，扩大可用性，并通过保险范围使该疗法变得更加实惠。

paras.en: “Our hope is that this research and technology can be a catalyst for more widespread development and innovation of more effective, personalized and precision-guided treatments,” Won said. “This is proof positive that population-scale personalized medicine is not just an aspirational goal but is an achievable reality today.”
paras.zh: Won 说：“我们希望这项研究和技术能够成为更有效、个性化和精确指导治疗的更广泛开发和创新的催化剂。” “这证明人口规模的个性化医疗不仅是一个理想的目标，而且是当今可以实现的现实。”

paras.en: The project combines years of work across medicine, neuroscience, clinical research, and technology, all directed toward improving the lives of people affected by PTSD.
paras.zh: 该项目结合了医学、神经科学、临床研究和技术领域多年的工作，所有这些都旨在改善受创伤后应激障碍 (PTSD) 影响的人们的生活。

paras.en: For Ramos, the opportunity to help veterans carries particular significance because of Texas A&M's longstanding involvement in military and veteran initiatives.
paras.zh: 对于拉莫斯来说，帮助退伍军人的机会具有特别重要的意义，因为德克萨斯农工大学长期参与军事和退伍军人倡议。

paras.en: “Texas A&M has a very rich history of military and veteran priorities,” Ramos said. “It’s a no-brainer that Texas A&M faculty would be interested in and supportive of an initiative that hopefully would bring positive solutions to a big problem. And anything we could do to help alleviate that problem is going to go a long way towards making a difference in the individual’s life as well as the people who are close to them. I feel very fortunate that we at Texas A&M were meaningfully involved in this project.”
paras.zh: “德克萨斯农工大学在军事和退伍军人优先事项方面有着非常丰富的历史，”拉莫斯说。 “毫无疑问，德州农工大学的教员会对一项有望为大问题带来积极解决方案的倡议感兴趣并支持。我们可以采取的任何措施来帮助缓解这个问题，都将大大有助于改变个人以及与他们关系密切的人的生活。我感到非常幸运，我们德州农工大学有意义地参与了这个项目。”

paras.en: Materials provided by Texas A&M University. Original written by Lasha Markham. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由德克萨斯农工大学提供。原创作者：拉莎·马卡姆。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: Dental implants can hijack your immune system, scientists discover

paras.en: Dental implants can hijack your immune system, scientists discover
paras.zh: 科学家发现，种植牙可以劫持你的免疫系统

paras.en: - Researchers have uncovered a surprising reason dental implant infections often resist antibiotics: the implants themselves can contribute to the problem. Bacteria corrode titanium implants, releasing microscopic particles that hijack immune cells, trigger destructive inflammation, and accelerate jawbone loss.
paras.zh: - 研究人员发现了种植牙感染通常对抗生素产生耐药性的一个令人惊讶的原因：种植体本身可能会导致这一问题。细菌腐蚀钛植入物，释放出劫持免疫细胞的微小颗粒，引发破坏性炎症，并加速颌骨损失。

paras.en: For tens of millions of people, dental implants have provided a way to replace missing teeth with a full set of fixed, functional teeth rather than removable dentures. However, an estimated 10% to 20% of implant patients eventually develop peri-implantitis, a serious infection that damages the surrounding jawbone.
paras.zh: 对于数以千万计的人来说，种植牙提供了一种用全套固定的、功能性的牙齿而不是活动假牙替代缺失牙齿的方法。然而，估计有 10% 至 20% 的种植体患者最终会出现种植体周围炎，这是一种会损害周围颌骨的严重感染。

paras.en: Antibiotics frequently fail to control this condition, and scientists have struggled to understand why. Now, researchers believe they have uncovered the mechanism responsible.
paras.zh: 抗生素经常无法控制这种情况，科学家们一直在努力理解其中的原因。现在，研究人员相信他们已经发现了造成这一现象的机制。

paras.en: A new study published in PNAS Nexus by scientists at the Rutgers School of Dental Medicine reveals that bacteria can gradually corrode dental implants, releasing microscopic titanium particles into nearby tissues. These particles interfere with the immune cells responsible for fighting infection, trapping them in a state of excessive inflammation that progressively destroys jawbone.
