paras.en: Having decoded the signals from some input device, such as the switch, one then has to broadcast it in a form people can understand. This could be visually, with text or diagrams on the screen. But if you want to communicate like others, which is what people in my position would like, you need to speak.
paras.zh: 对来自某些输入设备（例如开关）的信号进行解码后，必须以人们可以理解的形式进行广播。这可以是视觉上的，在屏幕上显示文本或图表。但如果你想像其他人一样沟通，这就是我这个职位的人所希望的，你就需要说话。

paras.en: Sanders: The late physicist Stephen Hawking had one of perhaps the most iconic computerized voices. Here he is giving a talk in 1994 at MIT.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：已故物理学家斯蒂芬·霍金的声音也许是最具标志性的计算机声音之一。这是 1994 年他在麻省理工学院发表的演讲。

paras.en: [Hawking audio] Computerized speech synthesizers have improved a great deal in recent years, and this is important. Not only does one want to be understood, but also one doesn’t want to sound like Mickey Mouse or a Dalek.
paras.zh: [霍金音频] 近年来，计算机语音合成器已经有了很大的改进，这一点很重要。人们不仅希望被理解，而且不想听起来像米老鼠或戴立克。

paras.en: Sanders: He’s describing his synthesized voice, which it turns out, he quite liked.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他正在描述他的合成声音，事实证明，他非常喜欢。

paras.en: [Hawking audio] This voice of mine may be a bit tinny and Irish, but it is almost human.
paras.zh: [霍金音频] 我的这个声音可能有点尖细和爱尔兰语，但它几乎是人类的。

paras.en: Sanders: Hawking was happy with that voice. Jules was not. Jules described his banked voice in a stand-up routine as sounding like if you played Daft Punk at quarter speed.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：霍金对这个声音很满意。朱尔斯不是。朱尔斯形容他在单口喜剧中的声音听起来就像你以四分之一的速度演奏《傻朋克》一样。

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] Okay, fast forward a bit, artificial intelligence came onto the scene. Now, with just short snippets of already recorded sound, these powerful programs can create synthetic voices with appropriate umms, breaths, sounds, and cadence that are very close to the original. These voices are so realistic that sometimes you can’t even hear the difference.
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆]好的，快进一点，人工智能出现了。现在，只需已录制的声音的一小段，这些强大的程序就可以创建具有适当的嗯、呼吸、声音和节奏的合成声音，非常接近原始声音。这些声音是如此真实，有时你甚至听不出区别。

paras.en: Sanders: Maybe you just noticed something, but maybe you didn’t. Those previous three sentences weren’t spoken by me at all. They were said by a voice clone I made. Okay, one more time. This is me talking.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：也许你刚刚注意到了一些事情，但也许你没有。前面三句话根本就不是我说的。这些是我制作的语音克隆说的。好吧，再来一次。这是我在说话。

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] And this is my voice clone.
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆]这是我的声音克隆。

paras.en: Sanders: I used ElevenLabs to clone my voice. That’s a company that uses AI technology to create lifelike, digital replicas of voices. To do it, I used the professional option, which required 30 minutes of audio to make. So for input, I recorded myself reading a few podcast scripts.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我用 ElevenLabs 克隆了我的声音。这是一家利用人工智能技术创建逼真的数字声音复制品的公司。为此，我使用了专业选项，需要制作 30 分钟的音频。因此，为了输入，我记录了自己阅读一些播客脚本的情况。

paras.en: Jules Rodriguez’s voice was disappearing.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯·罗德里格斯的声音消失了。

paras.en: Sanders: Some really long texts from my mom.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我妈妈发来的一些很长的短信。

paras.en: I’m at Food Lion. I’m getting pickles, half and half.
paras.zh: 我在Food Lion。我买的是泡菜，一半一半。

paras.en: Sanders: And chapter nine of Anne of Green Gables.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：还有《绿山墙的安妮》第九章。

paras.en: It’s a good thing Rachel Lynde got a calling down. She’s a meddlesome old gossip.
paras.zh: 雷切尔·林德接到电话是件好事。她是个爱管闲事的老八卦者。

paras.en: Sanders: After a few minutes, poof, there it was, my voice clone. It was spooky how much it sounded like me. I spent a fun afternoon playing with it. You can control so many different parts.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：几分钟后，噗，我的声音克隆出现了。听起来很像我，真是令人毛骨悚然。我和它一起度过了一个愉快的下午。您可以控制许多不同的部分。

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] It can speak quickly. And it can speak slowly. My voice clone can laugh. It can be utterly bored. It can also scoff when it thinks something is ridiculous. It can be menacing on Laura’s behalf.
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆]它可以快速说话。而且它可以慢慢地说话。我的声音克隆可以笑。它可能会非常无聊。当它认为某件事很荒谬时，它也会嘲笑。这对劳拉来说可能是一种威胁。

paras.en: Sanders: I could even speak fluent French.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我什至能说流利的法语。

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] Il peut même parler d’autres langues.
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆] Il peut même parler d’autres langues。

paras.en: Sanders: The technology uses a few different types of artificial intelligence at different stages. It extracts features of my voice, such as my pitch and tone, my prosody, even my breathing patterns. This lets it build a model of my voice, and then that model can be let loose to say anything I type. I got the idea from speech pathologist Kate Nilson, who has tried it herself.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：该技术在不同阶段使用了几种不同类型的人工智能。它提取我的声音特征，例如我的音调和语气、我的韵律，甚至我的呼吸模式。这让它构建了我的声音模型，然后可以让该模型说出我输入的任何内容。我从言语病理学家凯特·尼尔森那里得到了这个想法，她自己也尝试过。

paras.en: Nilson: We’ve even played the game of like, is it really me talking or is it the computer? And it’s kind of scary how realistic the computerized version of my voice is. The really awesome part about the voice cloning process is that you take recordings and submit that. It’s not like you record it right now. You take old recordings. And so for people you know for instance people living with ALS, if their speech is the first thing that’s affected and their speech has already changed, it might be too late to do the recordings, but if they have old voicemails or a speech that they gave or a podcast that they were on, something like that, then we can take those recordings and submit them to make a voice. And so that’s really opened a lot of doors for a lot of people.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：我们甚至玩过类似的游戏，到底是我在说话还是计算机在说话？我的声音的电脑版本如此真实，有点可怕。语音克隆过程中真正令人惊叹的部分是您录制并提交录音。这不像你现在就记录下来。你拿旧录音。因此，对于您认识的人，例如患有 ALS 的人，如果他们的言语是第一个受到影响的人，并且他们的言语已经发生了变化，那么进行录音可能为时已晚，但如果他们有旧的语音邮件或他们发表的演讲或他们正在收听的播客，类似的东西，那么我们可以获取这些录音并提交它们以制作声音。这确实为很多人打开了很多大门。

paras.en: Sanders: In June of 2024, Jules used recordings of his own voice to create an AI-generated voice clone, also through the company ElevenLabs.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2024 年 6 月，朱尔斯使用自己的录音创建了人工智能生成的语音克隆，也是通过 ElevenLabs 公司实现的。

paras.en: Jules: When I first heard my cloned voice, it felt like I reappeared. When my wife first heard it, she cried because of how close it sounded like me before I lost my voice.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：当我第一次听到我的克隆声音时，感觉就像我重新出现了一样。当我妻子第一次听到这首歌时，她哭了，因为这听起来太像我失声之前的我了。

paras.en: Sanders: After months of gradually hearing Jules’ voice less and less, his family had gotten used to the new normal. The voice clone was a big change.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：几个月来，朱尔斯的声音越来越少，他的家人已经习惯了新常态。声音克隆是一个很大的变化。

paras.en: Jules: They were all shocked at first, but now it just feels natural. It’s pretty crazy.
paras.zh: Jules：一开始他们都很震惊，但现在感觉很自然。这太疯狂了。

paras.en: Sanders: When you first started using the voice clone, do you remember what the first thing you said was? Were there things you really wanted to say?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当你第一次开始使用语音克隆时，你还记得你说的第一句话是什么吗？有什么你真的想说的话吗？

paras.en: Jules: Well, it was probably the cheesiest thing. I remember telling my wife how much I love her.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：嗯，这可能是最俗气的事情了。我记得告诉我的妻子我有多爱她。

paras.en: Sanders: Here’s how his wife MA remembers it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：以下是他妻子 MA 的回忆。

paras.en: MA: The first thing he played for me, I was like chills all over. And it was, it was incredibly beautiful and incredible and like, wow. And also I cried because it felt like there was a part of him that I was getting back that I had lost a long time ago.
paras.zh: MA：他为我演奏的第一首曲子，我浑身发冷。确实如此，它非常美丽，令人难以置信，就像，哇。我也哭了，因为我感觉他的一部分我很久以前就失去了，现在我又回来了。

paras.en: Sanders: It was surprisingly hard to get this one thing back in the middle of so much loss.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在如此巨大的损失中要挽回这一件事是出乎意料的困难。

paras.en: MA: It felt confusing emotionally to get that part back and not the rest of him back. Like, I just I feel it right now in my body as I talk about it. Things with ALS change so quickly and the voice is something so intimate you’re sort of like, you’re training yourself little by little to adapt and then all of a sudden this like really vibrant part of him came back, but everything else was the same. But that vibrant voice part came back and it was like, yeah. It was a bizarre experience but ultimately really, really special for us and for his son too.
paras.zh: MA：在情感上感到困惑的是要找回那部分而不是他的其他部分。就像，当我谈论它时，我现在就在我的身体里感受到了它。患有 ALS 的事情变化得如此之快，声音是如此亲密，你有点像，你正在一点一点地训练自己去适应，然后突然之间，他身上充满活力的部分又回来了，但其他一切都是一样的。但那个充满活力的声音部分又回来了，就像是，是的。这是一次奇怪的经历，但最终对我们和他的儿子来说真的非常特别。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules immediately took off the training wheels.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯立即取下辅助轮。

paras.en: Jules: I just wanted to explore the limits of it.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我只是想探索它的局限性。

paras.en: Sanders: In fact, Jules’ voice clone sounded so good that he decided his dream of doing stand up comedy was possible, long after he had given up the idea.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实上，朱尔斯的声音克隆听起来非常好，以至于在他放弃这个想法很久之后，他决定做单口喜剧的梦想是可能的。

paras.en: Jules: I started to write jokes with it pretty soon after hearing it.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我听到它后很快就开始用它写笑话。

paras.en: Sanders: So Jules started working on a set.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以朱尔斯开始制作一套。

paras.en: MA: When he tested the AI voice, it’s like a little light bulb went off and he was like, I think I could do comedy again. And I remember hearing that and going like, oh, my God, like that’s such a huge like thing to, to, it’s like you come alive in a new way, is what I saw through his eyes. He was like, I think I can do comedy again. I was like, wow.
paras.zh: MA：当他测试人工智能语音时，就像一个小灯泡熄灭了，他说，我想我可以再次出演喜剧。我记得听到这句话后，我就想，哦，天啊，这是一件多么巨大的事情，就像你以一种新的方式活过来一样，这就是我通过他的眼睛看到的。他说，我想我可以再次演喜剧。我当时想，哇。

paras.en: Jules: Oh, man, thank you. I wasn’t even sure if I was going to make it out here. So many things could stop me from being here. Hospital stays, tracheostomy, broken elevator. And the biggest thing would be any step larger than two inches. I’m so happy to be here with you all.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：噢，伙计，谢谢你。我什至不确定我是否能走出这里。有很多事情可以阻止我来这里。住院、气管切开术、电梯坏了。最大的事情是任何大于两英寸的台阶。我很高兴能和大家在一起。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s tempting to think that this personalization shouldn’t matter much, that having a voice, any voice, would do the job. But it’s not true. Having a voice that sounds like your real voice does matter a tremendous amount.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人们很容易认为这种个性化应该不那么重要，拥有一个声音，任何声音，就可以完成这项工作。但这不是真的。拥有听起来像真实声音的声音确实非常重要。

paras.en: Karina Nagin: You need to communicate what you’re thinking, your health directives. You need to tell your loved ones you love them. But I think we didn’t realize what a huge impact your voice sounding like you, what a big piece of identity that was.
paras.zh: 卡琳娜·纳金（Karina Nagin）：您需要传达您的想法和健康指示。你需要告诉你所爱的人你爱他们。但我认为我们没有意识到你的声音听起来有多么巨大的影响，这是一个多么重要的身份。

paras.en: Sanders: Karina Nagin directs Bridging Voice, a nonprofit organization that helps people with ALS find and use communication technology. That includes voice clones from ElevenLabs. It’s the group that helped Jules clone his voice. She’s heard stories about how voice clones and the connections they bring back led people to reconsider their medical directives.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：卡琳娜·纳金 (Karina Nagin) 领导 Bridging Voice，这是一个帮助 ALS 患者寻找和使用通信技术的非营利组织。其中包括来自 ElevenLabs 的语音克隆。正是这个团队帮助朱尔斯克隆了他的声音。她听说过有关声音克隆及其带回的联系如何引导人们重新考虑他们的医疗指示的故事。

paras.en: Nagin: And people, once they received these voice clones, it was so life-altering that they were changing their health directives of what they wanted to do. Many people changed their health directives. They said, if I have this voice and I can sound like me, I can continue to communicate and feel like myself, I want to live longer. This is something that makes it worth living for me. I think our team didn’t realize how impactful it was going to be, but we’ve had people use these voice clones to tell their wedding vows. I got a testimonial from a grandmother the other day who just got her voice clone, and she said, I immediately called up my grandchildren, the youngest of who had never heard my real voice. And so this is the first time they were hearing my voice.
paras.zh: 纳金：人们一旦收到这些声音克隆，生活就会发生巨大的改变，以至于他们正在改变自己想做的事情的健康指示。许多人改变了他们的健康指示。他们说，如果我有这个声音，并且听起来像我，我就可以继续交流，感觉像我自己，我想活得更久。这对我来说是值得活下去的。我认为我们的团队没有意识到它会有多大的影响力，但我们已经让人们使用这些声音克隆来讲述他们的婚礼誓言。前几天，我收到了一位祖母的感言，她刚刚克隆了她的声音，她说，我立即给我的孙子们打电话，他们中最小的一个从未听过我的真实声音。这是他们第一次听到我的声音。

paras.en: Sanders: Nagin says her team was surprised by the impact on not just the person whose voice is restored, but on their families too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：纳金说，她的团队感到惊讶的是，这不仅对恢复声音的人产生了影响，而且对他们的家人也产生了影响。

paras.en: Nagin: We were so focused on people and giving them the ability to communicate. The idea that it sounds more like them or not, we said, oh, that’s a nice add-on, but that’s not really the core of it. But as soon as we gave that to people, we realized that is the core of it, your identity and feeling like yourself. And it’s not just for the patients, but it’s their family members.
paras.zh: Nagin：我们非常关注人并赋予他们沟通的能力。不管听起来是否更像他们，我们说，哦，这是一个很好的附加组件，但这并不是它的核心。但当我们把它交给人们时，我们意识到这就是它的核心，你的身份和感觉就像你自己。这不仅是为了患者，也是为了他们的家人。

paras.en: Sanders: A personalized voice, one that sounds like the old one, is more than an add-on.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：一种个性化的声音，一种听起来像旧声音的声音，不仅仅是一种附加功能。

paras.en: Nagin: Endless videos of people. I mean, we have one of a college-aged boy who’s hearing his father’s voice for the first time in two years, and he just breaks down. Like, this is, you know, they’re going through this horrific experience of this diagnosis. And to be able to actually connect with a family member and hear their voice again, I think it equally brings joy and comfort to the families as much as it does to the person who’s been diagnosed with ALS.
paras.zh: Nagin：无穷无尽的人们视频。我的意思是，我们有一个大学生男孩，两年来第一次听到父亲的声音，他崩溃了。就像，你知道，他们正在经历这种诊断的可怕经历。能够真正与家人联系并再次听到他们的声音，我认为这同样会给家人带来欢乐和安慰，就像给被诊断患有 ALS 的人一样。

paras.en: Sanders: ALS forces families to confront tough medical decisions about life and death. Jules and MA had thought very carefully about how they’d approach the future. What kind of medical interventions would he be OK with, and what kind would he not want? Big picture, what sort of life was worth living? Jules had been getting by with just an external oxygen mask to help keep his body going. He had decided that he didn’t want to take a next big step of having a tracheostomy, a life-extending procedure that leaves a small tube in his throat connected to a ventilator. With a trache tube, Jules would need round-the-clock care, and he would lose his voice permanently.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：ALS 迫使家庭面临有关生死的艰难医疗决定。朱尔斯和马云非常仔细地考虑了他们如何应对未来。他可以接受什么样的医疗干预，他不想要什么样的医疗干预？从大局来看，什么样的生活值得过？朱尔斯一直靠外部氧气面罩维持身体运转。他决定不再进行气管造口术，这是一种延长生命的手术，会在他的喉咙里留下一根与呼吸机相连的小管。有了气管插管，朱尔斯需要全天候护理，而且他将永远失声。

paras.en: MA: He was someone who didn’t want to do a tracheostomy. Like, he was opting for, once I’m done, like, that’s it. And that was our plan.
paras.zh: MA：他是一个不想做气管切开术的人。就像，他选择，一旦我完成，就这样。这就是我们的计划。

paras.en: Sanders: In the summer of 2024, not too long after he had cloned his voice, Jules had reached a very tough spot.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：2024 年夏天，在克隆自己的声音后不久，朱尔斯就陷入了一个非常艰难的境地。

paras.en: MA: September, we went to the hospital again and we had one evening where we really thought like that was it, like he was going to, he was going to pass away that night. I remember texting his family and saying, you know, I don’t know that it’s going to happen right now, but we’re, I feel like we’re really close. And he went through this like crisis moment. And then on the other side, when they were able to like stabilize him again, he looked at me and he was like, babe, well, if the tracheostomy can help me live, then I think I’d change my mind. I want to do it. Let’s talk to the doctors about it.
paras.zh: MA：九月，我们再次去了医院，有一天晚上我们真的以为就这样了，就像他会那样，那天晚上他就会去世。我记得给他的家人发短信说，你知道，我不知道现在会发生什么，但我觉得我们真的很亲密。他经历了这个危机时刻。然后在另一边，当他们能够再次稳定他的情况时，他看着我，他说，宝贝，好吧，如果气管切开术可以帮助我活下去，那么我想我会改变主意。我想做。让我们和医生谈谈吧。

paras.en: Sanders: This decision to have a trache tube placed in his throat meant that Jules’ voice, diminished as it already was, would be gone. Remember, this is a couple who built their relationship on long, deep talks. Their intimate, funny, thoughtful conversations were so meaningful to them that they started an entire podcast based on them. But this decision, a proactive choice to fully and permanently lose the capacity to talk, represented a hard stop. A definitive end to talking. What you’re about to hear is a tough conversation. MA is telling me about a moment before the surgery.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在他的喉咙里放置气管插管的决定意味着朱尔斯的声音虽然已经减弱，但将会消失。请记住，这是一对通过长期深入的交谈建立了关系的夫妇。他们亲密、有趣、深思熟虑的对话对他们来说非常有意义，以至于他们基于这些对话开始了整个播客。但这一决定，是一种主动选择完全永久失去说话能力的决定，代表着一种硬性停止。谈话彻底结束。你将要听到的是一场艰难的对话。 MA 正在告诉我手术前一刻的情况。

paras.en: MA: So I remember the night, the day, yeah, he was, the operation was like in the evening when they did it, and me recording like a last little video of us talking because I was like, I just want to capture your voice one more time. And he was like, oh babe, you know, being all like, and I haven’t even looked at that video, but it’s there. And so that was a big, it was a big transition.
paras.zh: MA：所以我记得那天晚上，那天，是的，他是，手术就像在晚上，他们做的时候，我录下了我们谈话的最后一个小视频，因为我想，我只是想再一次捕捉到你的声音。他说，哦宝贝，你知道，就像，我什至没有看过那个视频，但它就在那里。所以这是一个很大的转变。

paras.en: Sanders: You can’t see it, of course, but maybe you can hear it. As we talk, we’re both crying.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当然，你看不到它，但也许你能听到它。当我们说话时，我们都在哭。

paras.en: MA: I think I mentioned when we spoke last time how of all the things from the very beginning that I was like, oh, he’s going to lose the ability to this and this and this and this and this. I was like, oh, my God, when he loses the ability to speak, like, I’m going to really, really, really, really, really have a hard time. And all of the abrupt changes and the way you have to adapt to them kind of prepare you for the next things. And so usually the fear of the thing happening is more than when it actually happens. And then you’re there and you’re like, okay, we’re here and we’ll adapt to it. That’s usually been the case for pretty much everything. But yeah, it was big.
paras.zh: MA：我想我在上次谈话时提到过，从一开始我就想，哦，他将失去这个、这个、这个、这个、这个的能力。我当时想，哦，天哪，当他失去说话的能力时，我会真的，真的，真的，真的，真的很难过。所有突然的变化以及你必须适应它们的方式都在为你接下来的事情做好准备。因此，通常情况下，人们对事情发生的恐惧比事情真正发生时的恐惧要多。然后你就在那里，你会说，好吧，我们在这里，我们会适应它。几乎所有事情通常都是如此。但是，是的，它很大。

paras.en: Sanders: But there was something that made the final and complete loss of Jules’ voice easier. Jules’ new digital voice. This was a very realistic AI-generated recreation of his old voice, the one that his family knew and loved. The existence of this new voice factored into Jules’ decision to get a trache.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是有一些事情让朱尔斯最终完全失去声音变得更容易。朱尔斯的新数字声音。这是人工智能对他的旧声音进行的非常逼真的再现，也是他的家人所熟悉和喜爱的声音。这个新声音的存在促使朱尔斯决定接受气管切开手术。

paras.en: MA: I really do believe that the AI voice and the ability for him to actually communicate in that way is one of the things that helped him decide to keep living.
paras.zh: MA：我确实相信人工智能的声音和他以这种方式进行实际交流的能力是帮助他决定继续生活的因素之一。

paras.en: Sanders: It wasn’t everything, of course. A decision like this depends on so many moving pieces. But it was big.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当然，这还不是全部。这样的决定取决于许多变化的因素。但它很大。

paras.en: MA: I firmly believe that it had an enormous positive impact in him considering it, like, as a way of you know having certain goals and experiences that he thought, you know, wouldn’t have been there, had it not been for the cloned voice. So I’ve I’ve gone as far to say that if it wasn’t for the clone voice, I don’t think he, I don’t think he would have chosen the trache. Yeah, then that moment anything could happen, but he was pretty, a pretty like no, I don’t want the tracheostomy kind of guy from the beginning. And then all of that changed. And so I think it was a huge driver.
paras.zh: MA：我坚信这对他的考虑产生了巨大的积极影响，就像，作为一种你知道拥有某些目标和经历的方式，他认为，如果没有克隆声音，这些目标和经历就不会存在。所以我想说的是，如果不是克隆人的声音，我认为他不会选择气管切开术。是的，在那一刻任何事情都可能发生，但他很漂亮，非常漂亮，不，我从一开始就不想要气管切开术那种人。然后一切都改变了。所以我认为这是一个巨大的推动力。

paras.en: Sanders: At the time of Jules’ hospitalization and surgery, they talked to their son Skylar about what was going on.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯住院并接受手术时，他们与儿子斯凯拉谈论了发生的事情。

paras.en: MA: The whole like communicating with him afterwards, because I said, you know, now he’s going to lose his voice completely. He’s like, we have the computer. That’s great. And I was like, okay, yeah, true. The things he’s told us over time are like bonkers. How he sees, the perspective he has on things, is incredible. So that was a really big, pivotal time for like what it means to like use your voice, to keep your voice, to fight for your voice and to express yourself in ways that you didn’t even think you would before. That takes a lot of courage and willingness.
paras.zh: MA：整个过程就像事后与他交流，因为我说，你知道，现在他将完全失去声音。他说，我们有电脑。那太棒了。我当时想，好吧，是的，是的。随着时间的推移，他告诉我们的事情就像疯了一样。他的看法、他对事物的看法令人难以置信。所以那是一个非常重要、关键的时刻，对于喜欢使用你的声音、保留你的声音、为你的声音而战以及以你以前从未想过的方式表达自己意味着什么意味着什么。这需要很大的勇气和意愿。

paras.en: Sanders: And what is your voice? I mean, to Skylar, it didn’t matter because his voice was still there.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：你的声音是什么？我的意思是，对于斯凯拉来说，这并不重要，因为他的声音仍然存在。

paras.en: Sanders: To Jules’ son, the voice clone was his dad’s voice. That’s really all there was to it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：对于朱尔斯的儿子来说，声音克隆就是他父亲的声音。这就是全部内容了。

paras.en: MA: He had his tracheostomy October, October 1st, and he was in the hospital for another two weeks. And then, mid-November, he was performing at, you know, an improv at one of our local comedy clubs.
paras.zh: MA：他于 10 月，10 月 1 日进行了气管造口术，然后又在医院呆了两周。然后，十一月中旬，他在我们当地的一个喜剧俱乐部进行即兴表演。

paras.en: Jules: In all seriousness, thanks for coming out. My name is Jules and because of the advancements in AI, I now have the ability to come up here and do this again with my original voice.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：说实话，感谢您的光临。我的名字是 Jules，由于人工智能的进步，我现在有能力来到这里，用我原来的声音再次做到这一点。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules was back. Jules, with his voice clone, can laugh and sing and start trouble with his wife.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯回来了。朱尔斯拥有他的声音克隆，可以笑、可以唱歌，还可以惹恼他的妻子。

paras.en: Jules: One thing in particular is how it inserts tone and inflections on words. Sometimes my wife will get mad because my response can come off with some sass.
paras.zh: Jules：特别的一件事是它如何在单词中插入语气和变化。有时我的妻子会生气，因为我的回答可能有些无礼。

paras.en: Sanders: I asked Jules if he can swear with it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我问朱尔斯他是否可以用它发誓。

paras.en: Jules: [Beep] yeah, I can. With the latest version of this technology, I have more control of how I sound with prompts. That includes laughing, whispering, and even singing. I could never sing, even though my wife and I met at a karaoke bar.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：[嘟嘟]是的，我可以。借助这项技术的最新版本，我可以更好地控制提示音的发音。这包括大笑、窃窃私语，甚至唱歌。我从来不会唱歌，尽管我和妻子是在卡拉 OK 酒吧认识的。

paras.en: Sanders: I think you can sing. Anyone who wants to sing can sing.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我认为你会唱歌。任何想唱歌的人都可以唱歌。

paras.en: Sanders: Cave has been a speech therapist for decades, but even he was won over by the capabilities of these newer AI-generated voice clones.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯夫几十年来一直是一名言语治疗师，但即使是他也被这些新的人工智能生成的语音克隆的能力所折服。

paras.en: Cave: I was really pleasantly surprised. These voices were the most authentic sounding I’d ever heard from this technology. It actually sounded like the people I was working with. And so it really changed my world. And because I was known for voice banking, I was getting a lot of inquiries. And I ended up spending so much time on answering questions about ElevenLabs. What really, really excited me was that many people reported that their social networks was being strengthened again, that more people were coming to talk to them and to reflect on times past and times current. And that to me is gold. That’s what voice banking is or should be, to maintain social and work networks.
paras.zh: Cave：我真的很惊喜。这些声音是我从这项技术中听到过的最真实的声音。实际上听起来就像和我一起工作的人。所以它确实改变了我的世界。因为我以语音银行闻名，所以我收到了很多询问。我最终花了很多时间来回答有关 ElevenLabs 的问题。 What really, really excited me was that many people reported that their social networks was being strengthened again, that more people were coming to talk to them and to reflect on times past and times current.这对我来说就是黄金。这就是语音银行的作用，或者应该是维持社交和工作网络的作用。

paras.en: Sanders: I’d say that we’ve now gone well beyond almost human, as Stephen Hawking put it. Today’s voice clones are fluid, individual, and in many ways, seamless. My synthetic voice says certain words the exact same way I would say them.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我想说，正如斯蒂芬·霍金所说，我们现在已经远远超出了人类的范畴。今天的声音克隆是流畅的、个性化的，而且在很多方面都是无缝的。我的合成声音说出某些单词的方式与我说它们的方式完全相同。

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] My real voice says certain words the exact same way I would say them. It’s spooky.
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆]我的真实声音说某些词的方式与我说的方式完全相同。太诡异了。

paras.en: Sanders: The stories I’ve heard of how people are using these voices back this up. I emailed with Peggy Merrill, who lost her voice from ALS. She uses her voice clone to read to her grandkids, teach yoga, and lead guided meditation.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我听到的关于人们如何使用这些声音的故事支持了这一点。我给佩吉·梅里尔发了电子邮件，她因肌萎缩侧索硬化症失去了声音。她用她的声音克隆给她的孙子读书、教瑜伽，并引导冥想。

paras.en: Sanders: Peggy wrote to me, “It renews my sense of self to use and hear my own voice.” And there’s Patrick Darling, who you heard from in an earlier episode. He’s a composer and musician, and he’s been writing new songs and performing them with his voice clone.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：佩吉写信给我说，“使用和听到自己的声音让我重新认识了自己。”还有帕特里克·达林（Patrick Darling），您在前一集中就听说过他。他是一位作曲家和音乐家，他一直在创作新歌曲并用他的声音克隆来表演。

paras.en: Patrick Darling: The first time I performed with the AI voice, I was surprised how physically connected I felt with it, even though I was not actually singing.
paras.zh: Patrick Darling：我第一次用人工智能声音表演时，我很惊讶我与它的身体联系，尽管我实际上并没有唱歌。

paras.en: Patrick: It’s hard to explain. There’s just this strange energy about it and you feel like a performer again.
paras.zh: 帕特里克：这很难解释。这里面有一种奇怪的能量，你感觉自己又像一个表演者了。

paras.en: Sanders: Patrick’s description of feeling physically connected to his voice, I think, might be a big hint about why this voice cloning technology is so powerful. These realistic voices are able to create connections both within people and between people. These connections were lost, and then they’re remade. And they matter because of not just the big heavy conversations, but the little everyday stuff too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我认为，帕特里克描述的感觉与他的声音有物理联系，这可能是一个很大的暗示，说明为什么这种声音克隆技术如此强大。这些真实的声音能够在人与人之间以及人与人之间建立联系。这些联系丢失了，然后又重新建立了。它们之所以重要，不仅因为重大的谈话，还因为日常的小事。

paras.en: Jules still has to use eye-tracking technology to type out what he wants to say. He has a device that senses where he’s looking on a screen and uses his gaze to write. Only then does his voice clone say what he wants it to say. That takes a lot of time and focus. Scientists are working on ways to get the words out faster by using signals earlier in the speech process.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯仍然需要使用眼球追踪技术来输入他想说的话。他有一个设备可以感知他在屏幕上看向的位置，并利用他的目光进行书写。只有这样，他的声音分身才会说出他想说的话。这需要大量的时间和注意力。科学家们正在研究如何通过在语音过程的早期使用信号来更快地说出单词。

paras.en: On the next episode…researchers want to pull words straight from the brain.
paras.zh: 在下一集中……研究人员想要直接从大脑中提取单词。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: And the more I read and I thought, why not me? And why not now?
paras.zh: 凯西·哈勒尔：我读得越多，思考得越多，为什么不是我呢？为什么不现在呢？

paras.en: Sanders: What does it feel like to have your thoughts turned into words?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：将你的想法变成文字是什么感觉？

paras.en: Leigh Hochberg: The first thing that he said was something along the lines of, you know, is this thing on? And then the second thing that we decoded was, I’m looking for a cheetah. And it’s the second day. You know, there’s no way that the second sentence on the second day of using an implanted brain computer interface is going to say anything about a cheetah. You know, that’s obviously a decoding error, and that’s fine. Except for the fact that his four-year-old daughter had just walked into the room dressed as a cheetah.
paras.zh: Leigh Hochberg：他说的第一句话是这样的，你知道，这件事还在吗？然后我们解码的第二件事是，我在寻找猎豹。而且已经是第二天了。你知道，使用植入脑机接口的第二天的第二句话不可能说任何关于猎豹的事情。你知道，这显然是一个解码错误，但没关系。除了他四岁的女儿刚刚打扮成猎豹走进房间。

paras.en: Sanders: This is The Deep End. Talk to me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast, tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这就是深渊。跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。

paras.en: Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Schute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特 (Nancy Schute) 是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: A quantum computing feat brings the ‘megaquops’ era a step closer
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: Quantum computers capable of doing a million reliable operations could bring about a new stage of quantum calculation. That “megaquop” regime — as it’s called — isn’t here yet. But scientists just took a significant step toward it.
paras.zh: 能够进行一百万次可靠运算的量子计算机可能会带来量子计算的新阶段。所谓的“巨型”政权尚未出现。但科学家们刚刚朝着这个目标迈出了重要的一步。

paras.en: A quantum computer built by the company Quantinuum has error rates so low that it could perform a million operations with only about five errors, researchers report in a paper posted October 19 on the company’s website and arXiv.org.
paras.zh: 研究人员在 10 月 19 日在该公司网站和 arXiv.org 上发布的一篇论文中报告称，Quantinuum 公司制造的量子计算机的错误率非常低，可以执行一百万次运算，而只有大约 5 个错误。

paras.en: “These statistics are consistent with this being a good building block for that megaquop machine,” says quantum physicist David Hayes of Quantinuum, who is based in Broomfield, Colo. In order to reach that regime, however, such computers will need to be scaled up.
paras.zh: 位于科罗拉多州布鲁姆菲尔德的 Quantinuum 公司的量子物理学家 David Hayes 表示：“这些统计数据表明，这是巨型机器的良好构建模块。”然而，为了达到这一目标，此类计算机需要扩大规模。

paras.en: Quantinuum’s computer, known as Helios, is made of electrically charged atoms, called ions, hovering over a chip. Those ions serve as the 98 quantum bits, or qubits, of the computer. But, like all qubits, those ions are finicky. Their states are delicate and can flip unintentionally and mess up calculations, like a 0 randomly switching to a 1.
paras.zh: Quantinuum 的计算机被称为 Helios，由悬浮在芯片上的带电原子（称为离子）组成。这些离子充当计算机的 98 个量子位。但是，像所有量子位一样，这些离子很挑剔。它们的状态很微妙，可能会无意中翻转并扰乱计算，就像 0 随机切换到 1 一样。

paras.en: A technique called quantum error correction tackles this by combining multiple error-prone qubits into one, forming a supercharged unit called a logical qubit that is less prone to mistakes. (For those who grew up on 1990s TV, it’s a bit like how Captain Planet is born from the combined powers of the gang of Planeteers.)
paras.zh: 一种称为量子纠错的技术通过将多个容易出错的量子位组合成一个来解决这个问题，形成一个称为逻辑量子位的增压单元，该单元不易出错。 （对于那些看着 20 世纪 90 年代电视长大的人来说，这有点像星球队长是由星球人团伙的力量联合诞生的。）

paras.en: Logical qubits come in different sizes, integrating a given number of physical qubits — the ions, in this case. Each time a logical qubit is scaled up, going, say, from seven physical qubits to 19, the error rate drops by a factor called lambda. A previous demonstration of error correction by Google, reported in Nature in 2024, had a lambda of about 2, meaning errors were cut in half each time the logical qubits were scaled up.
paras.zh: 逻辑量子位有不同的大小，集成了给定数量的物理量子位（在本例中为离子）。每次扩大逻辑量子位（例如从 7 个物理量子位到 19 个）时，错误率都会下降一个称为 lambda 的因子。 2024 年《自然》杂志报道了谷歌之前的纠错演示，其 lambda 约为 2，这意味着每次扩大逻辑量子位时，错误都会减少一半。

paras.en: Quantinuum’s computer has a lambda of about 10. So errors dropped quickly when the researchers made larger logical qubits. A logical qubit composed of 37 physical qubits had just 5 errors in a million operations — close to what would be needed for the megaquop regime. However, that experiment involved only a single logical qubit. Reaching the megaquop regime could possibly involve around 50 to 100 logical qubits.
paras.zh: Quantinuum 的计算机的 lambda 约为 10。因此，当研究人员制造出更大的逻辑量子位时，错误会迅速下降。由 37 个物理量子位组成的逻辑量子位在一百万次操作中仅出现 5 个错误——接近巨型量子体系所需的水平。然而，该实验仅涉及单个逻辑量子位。达到巨型量子状态可能需要大约 50 到 100 个逻辑量子位。

paras.en: The large value of lambda means that achieving a desired error rate takes fewer physical qubits, says Ken Brown, a quantum engineer at Duke University and a scientific adviser for the company Logiqal who was not involved with the research. “That’s a huge savings in the overall number of qubits you would need. So that’s what’s exciting.”
paras.zh: 杜克大学量子工程师、Logiqal 公司的科学顾问 Ken Brown（未参与这项研究）表示，lambda 值较大意味着实现所需的错误率需要更少的物理量子位。 “这大大节省了您所需的量子比特总数。所以这就是令人兴奋的地方。”

articles.title: Rule breaking by just a few people can be contagious
articles.author: Sujata Gupta

paras.en: On the long drive to my kid’s sporting event this weekend, most drivers, myself included, cruised a few miles over the speed limit. A few drivers, though, blazed past in the left lane. Mindful of safety — and police cruisers — I didn’t follow suit.
paras.zh: 本周末，在我孩子参加体育赛事的长途驾驶中，大多数司机（包括我自己）都超速行驶了几英里。不过，有几名司机在左侧车道上超车了。考虑到安全和警车，我没有效仿。

paras.en: Left unchecked though, a few bad actors can trigger social breakdown, researchers report October 21 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The truly deviant among us “basically take off the guardrails of the group,” says Lucas Molleman, a psychologist at the University of Amsterdam.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 10 月 21 日在《英国皇家学会学报 B》上报道称，如果不加以控制，一些不良行为者可能会引发社会崩溃。阿姆斯特丹大学心理学家卢卡斯·莫勒曼 (Lucas Molleman) 表示，我们当中真正的越轨者“基本上会脱离群体的护栏”。

paras.en: Molleman and his colleagues designed a thought experiment to show what it takes to sway people to bend or break the rules. They picked a contentious time: A week before the 2024 U.S. presidential election. The team recruited 750 U.S. participants, with roughly half identifying as Democrats and half as Republicans. The online participants watched an animated shooting star streak across a row of 100 squares and then selected which square shone the brightest.
paras.zh: 莫勒曼和他的同事设计了一个思想实验，以展示如何影响人们改变或打破规则。他们选择了一个有争议的时间：2024 年美国总统大选前一周。该团队招募了 750 名美国参与者，其中大约一半是民主党人，一半是共和党人。在线参与者观看动画流星划过一排 100 个方格，然后选择哪个方格最亮。

paras.en: Though the brightest square always appeared around the row’s middle, participants received more money for selecting squares farther to the right (the farthest-right square netted participants roughly the equivalent of $1.30). Dedicated rule followers, or those who always followed the rules, and rule breakers, existed in roughly equal numbers, with each comprising about a fifth of the larger group, initial tests showed.
paras.zh: 虽然最亮的方块总是出现在该行的中间，但参与者选择更右边的方块会获得更多的钱（最右边的方块为参与者带来的净收益大约相当于 1.30 美元）。初步测试显示，专心遵守规则的人，或者说始终遵守规则的人，与规则破坏者的数量大致相等，各占较大群体的约五分之一。

paras.en: The researchers then stirred the pot. Participants repeated the simple experiment several times while receiving information about a previous respondent, including their political affiliation and level of adherence to the rule. Rule followers rarely begot more rule followers, even when respondents belonged to the same political party, the team found.
paras.zh: 然后研究人员搅拌锅。参与者多次重复这个简单的实验，同时收到有关先前受访者的信息，包括他们的政治立场和遵守规则的程度。研究小组发现，即使受访者属于同一政党，规则追随者也很少会产生更多的规则追随者。

paras.en: The reverse held true for rule breakers, though. Receiving information that someone with the same political leanings had just disregarded the rules shifted selections rightward on average. Absent social cues, participants selected the farthest-right square roughly 23 percent of the time. That increased to almost 40 percent of the time after participants learned that a political comrade had made the most lucrative choice. Bad behavior, in other words, was contagious.
paras.zh: 不过，对于规则破坏者来说，情况恰恰相反。收到具有相同政治倾向的人无视规则的信息后，平均选择会向右移动。在没有社交线索的情况下，参与者大约 23% 的时间选择了最右边的方块。在参与者得知政治同志做出了最有利可图的选择后，这种情况增加到近 40%。换句话说，不良行为具有传染性。

paras.en: Most individuals’ rule-breaking levels mirrored or stayed below that of others. But just over 4 percent of individuals escalated deviant behavior beyond that of the previous respondent.
paras.zh: 大多数人的违规程度与其他人相同或低于其他人。但只有超过 4% 的人将异常行为升级，超过了之前的受访者。

paras.en: The researchers then created a computer simulation to see how those rule-breaking behaviors might play out across time. They designed a digital twin for each of the 750 participants and had the doppelgängers interact in groups of 100. In some scenarios, those few escalation-prone individuals could push everyone in the group toward wild rule breaking. But if the 100-twin selection had the same proportion of dedicated rule followers as the human experiment, overall deviance settled at a more intermediate level.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员创建了一个计算机模拟，以了解这些违反规则的行为随着时间的推移可能会如何发挥作用。他们为 750 名参与者每人设计了一个数字孪生体，并让分身以 100 人为一组进行互动。在某些情况下，这几个容易升级的个体可能会促使小组中的每个人疯狂违反规则。但如果 100 名双胞胎的选择具有与人类实验相同比例的专门规则追随者，则总体偏差会稳定在更中间的水平。

paras.en: This study provides some keen insights into how humans might behave absent consequences, says behavioral economist Eugen Dimant of the University of Pennsylvania. “But that’s not how the world works.” His work suggests that to truly understand social contagion and the emergence of mobs, researchers must consider societal forces, such as punishments and social norms, that tend to keep behavior in check.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学的行为经济学家尤金·迪曼特表示，这项研究为人类在没有后果的情况下如何表现提供了一些敏锐的见解。 “但这不是世界运转的方式。”他的工作表明，要真正理解社会传染和暴民的出现，研究人员必须考虑社会力量，例如惩罚和社会规范，这些力量往往会控制行为。

paras.en: To Molleman, though, the study’s insights into individual behaviors are key. This pared-down experiment shows how just a few bad actors can cause entire groups to spiral out of control. Such findings could underpin everything from collective speeding to peaceful protests that turn violent, he says. “This is fundamental science … Obviously reality is way more complex.”
paras.zh: 不过，对于莫勒曼来说，这项研究对个人行为的洞察是关键。这个简化的实验表明，仅仅几个坏人就可以导致整个群体失控。他说，这些发现可以为从集体超速到演变为暴力的和平抗议等一切行为提供依据。 “这是基础科学……显然现实要复杂得多。”

articles.title: Scientists Just Cracked a Quantum Mystery That's Puzzled Physicists For Decades
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: The Kondo effect is one of the most important in quantum physics, describing the strange interference that magnetic atoms can have in metals.
paras.zh: 近藤效应是量子物理学中最重要的效应之一，描述了磁性原子在金属中可能产生的奇怪干扰。

paras.en: Usually, as metals cool, they become better at conducting electricity, because the reduction in energy means electrons can flow more smoothly. Add in a magnetic atom or two, though, and below a certain temperature (the Kondo temperature), electrical resistance starts to rise again.
paras.zh: 通常，随着金属冷却，它们的导电能力会变得更好，因为能量的减少意味着电子可以更顺畅地流动。然而，添加一两个磁性原子，在低于一定温度（近藤温度）时，电阻开始再次上升。

paras.en: That's the Kondo effect, and we already know a lot about it. But in a physics first, researchers from the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) and Yale University in the US have managed to precisely quantify the effect in a real material via fundamental physics calculations.
paras.zh: 这就是近藤效应，我们已经对此了解很多。但首先在物理学方面，来自美国加州理工学院 (Caltech) 和耶鲁大学的研究人员已经成功通过基础物理计算精确量化了真实材料中的效应。

paras.en: The work, published in Science, represents a significant step forward. Previously, scientists had to use real-world experiments and simplified models to pin down the Kondo effect, without getting predictions as precise as the new method.
paras.zh: 这项发表在《科学》杂志上的研究代表着向前迈出的重要一步。此前，科学家们必须使用现实世界的实验和简化的模型来确定近藤效应，而无法获得像新方法那样精确的预测。

paras.en: "It is now possible to predict the properties of some complicated materials purely through computation without referring to experiments," says physicist Garnet Chan, from Caltech.
paras.zh: 加州理工学院的物理学家 Garnet Chan 表示：“现在可以纯粹通过计算来预测一些复杂材料的特性，而无需参考实验。”

paras.en: Scientists already know what causes the Kondo effect. Electrons swarm around the magnetic impurities in the metal, canceling out the magnetism of the atoms and impeding electrical flow at the same time.
paras.zh: Scientists already know what causes the Kondo effect.电子聚集在金属中的磁性杂质周围，抵消了原子的磁性，同时阻碍了电流。

paras.en: "That is the signature of the Kondo effect, and it's a property of the electrons in the impurity interacting with the electrons traveling through the bulk metal," says Chan.
paras.zh: “这是近藤效应的特征，它是杂质中的电子与穿过块体金属的电子相互作用的特性，”陈说。

paras.en: Knowing what's going on isn't the same as being able to model it with full precision, though. Such are the complexities of the electron interactions in this 'many-body problem' that it's very tricky to predict when the flip in resistance will happen for different combinations of metals and magnetic impurities.
paras.zh: 不过，了解正在发生的事情并不等同于能够完全精确地对其进行建模。这种“多体问题”中电子相互作用的复杂性使得预测金属和磁性杂质的不同组合何时会发生电阻翻转非常棘手。

paras.en: Temperatures, electron spins, and magnetism all interact at incredibly small scales in these materials as the Kondo effect takes hold. It's way beyond the capabilities of even the most powerful supercomputers.
paras.zh: 当近藤效应出现时，温度、电子自旋和磁性都会在这些材料中以令人难以置信的小尺度相互作用。即使是最强大的超级计算机也无法做到这一点。

paras.en: To overcome the challenges, the researchers adopted an ab initio ('from first principles') approach. They borrowed techniques from chemistry to more fully model a single magnetic atom, without simplification, as if it were a larger molecule.
paras.zh: 为了克服这些挑战，研究人员采用了从头开始（“从第一原理开始”）的方法。他们借用了化学技术，更全面地模拟了单个磁性原子，没有进行简化，就好像它是一个更大的分子一样。

paras.en: With the help of some mathematical shortcuts and a lot of computer time, they then applied the basic laws of quantum physics to this newly modeled magnetic atom, repeating calculations again and again to narrow down their predictions.
paras.zh: 然后，在一些数学捷径和大量计算机时间的帮助下，他们将量子物理的基本定律应用于这个新建模的磁性原子，一次又一次地重复计算以缩小他们的预测范围。

paras.en: By comparing the modeling quantifications with lab measurements of the Kondo effect, the researchers proved the high level of accuracy of their prediction system. In some cases, the new approach was 100 times more accurate than current, simplified modeling.
paras.zh: 通过将建模量化与近藤效应的实验室测量结果进行比较，研究人员证明了他们的预测系统的高度准确性。在某些情况下，新方法比当前的简化建模准确 100 倍。

paras.en: The researchers picked the most basic examples of metals and magnetic atom combinations here – but further down the line, there's the potential to study increasingly complex materials.
paras.zh: 研究人员在这里选择了金属和磁性原子组合的最基本的例子——但更进一步，有可能研究日益复杂的材料。

paras.en: "These first materials that we have studied are like a baby step, or a prototype problem, along the way to more complex phenomena such as high-temperature superconductors and quantum magnets," says Chan.
paras.zh: 陈说：“我们研究的这些第一批材料就像一个婴儿步骤，或者一个原型问题，一直到更复杂的现象，如高温超导体和量子磁体。”

paras.en: Better prediction methods mean scientists can more confidently develop and investigate materials, such as superconductors, that promise to transform the systems we use for power grids and large-scale computing.
paras.zh: 更好的预测方法意味着科学家可以更加自信地开发和研究超导体等材料，这些材料有望改变我们用于电网和大规模计算的系统。

paras.en: The materials with the most potential tend to also have the most complex electron behaviors – which is where the methods used in this study could help.
paras.zh: 最具潜力的材料往往也具有最复杂的电子行为——这正是本研究中使用的方法可以提供帮助的地方。

paras.en: There's still a lot of progress to be made, but now that the approach has been shown to work, the researchers can begin to scale it up, giving scientists a tool to study complex quantum material behaviors without having to get lab data first.
paras.zh: 仍有很多进展需要取得，但现在该方法已被证明有效，研究人员可以开始扩大规模，为科学家提供一个研究复杂量子材料行为的工具，而无需先获取实验室数据。

paras.en: "We are in an exciting era in which faithful predictive quantum descriptions of the full chemical complexity of real materials are coming within reach," says chemist Linqing Peng, from Caltech.
paras.zh: 加州理工学院的化学家彭林清说：“我们正处于一个激动人心的时代，对真实材料的完整化学复杂性进行忠实的预测性量子描述已经成为可能。”

paras.en: "It is becoming realistic to predict material-specific behavior of correlated electrons from first principles, even in some of the most challenging classes of quantum materials."
paras.zh: “从第一原理预测相关电子的特定材料行为变得越来越现实，即使是在一些最具挑战性的量子材料类别中。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学》杂志上。

articles.title: One Habit May Delay Ovarian Aging – And a Drug Could Mimic Its Effects
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: The ovaries are among the first organs to show signs of aging, and yet we still don't really know why or how to slow down the inevitable.
paras.zh: 卵巢是最先出现衰老迹象的器官之一，但我们仍然不知道为什么或如何减缓不可避免的衰老迹象。

paras.en: No currently approved therapies can slow ovarian aging.
paras.zh: 目前没有批准的疗法可以减缓卵巢衰老。

paras.en: But new research among humans and mice has now identified a treatment that possibly could – one that's accessible to the vast majority of us.
paras.zh: 但针对人类和小鼠的新研究现在已经确定了一种可能可行的治疗方法——一种我们绝大多数人都可以使用的治疗方法。

paras.en: In experiments among female mice, those that regularly exercised on a treadmill for one month, as opposed to those that didn't, had more follicles in their ovaries.
paras.zh: 在对雌性小鼠进行的实验中，那些经常在跑步机上锻炼一个月的小鼠，与那些没有锻炼的小鼠相比，其卵巢中有更多的卵泡。

paras.en: They also showed a lower loss of primordial follicles, which are dormant eggs that cannot be replaced. They represent the ovary's reserve of immature oocytes.
paras.zh: 他们还表现出原始卵泡的损失较少，原始卵泡是无法替代的休眠卵。它们代表卵巢储备的未成熟卵母细胞。

paras.en: What's even more exciting, however, is that there's a drug that can replicate these reproductive benefits, even without exercise.
paras.zh: 然而，更令人兴奋的是，有一种药物即使不运动也能复制这些生殖益处。

paras.en: When mice were injected with an experimental drug called AdipoRon, it extended their reproductive lifespan, and they went on to have offspring later in life than untreated mice.
paras.zh: 当给小鼠注射一种名为 AdipoRon 的实验药物时，它们的生殖寿命得以延长，而且它们比未接受治疗的小鼠生育后代的时间也更长。

paras.en: With these injections, the number of total ovarian follicles and the protein levels of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) were significantly higher.
paras.zh: 通过这些注射，卵泡总数和抗苗勒氏管激素（AMH）的蛋白质水平显着升高。

paras.en: Most untreated mice stopped reproducing around 12 months of age.
paras.zh: 大多数未经治疗的小鼠在 12 个月大时停止繁殖。

paras.en: But mice treated with AdipoRon continued producing offspring until they were up to 15 months of age.
paras.zh: 但接受 AdipoRon 治疗的小鼠继续产生后代，直到它们长到 15 个月大。

paras.en: The research, led by scientists at Guangzhou Medical University in China, was published in Nature Aging.
paras.zh: 这项研究由中国广州医科大学的科学家领导，发表在《自然衰老》杂志上。

paras.en: "By confirming the protective effects of physical activity on ovarian aging, this study contributes to the broader understanding that physical activity can delay the aging process in multiple organs," the authors write in their paper, led by biomedical researchers Biao Li, Nana Zheng, and Tong Luo.
paras.zh: 由生物医学研究人员 Biao Li、Nana Cheng 和 Tong Luo 领导的论文作者在论文中写道：“通过证实体力活动对卵巢衰老的保护作用，这项研究有助于更广泛地理解体力活动可以延缓多个器官的衰老过程。”

paras.en: According to biochemist Philipp Scherer, who was not involved in the study, this research "is a well-performed, very exciting addition to the field."
paras.zh: 未参与这项研究的生物化学家菲利普·谢勒 (Philipp Scherer) 表示，这项研究“是该领域的一项出色的、非常令人兴奋的补充”。

paras.en: Today, there are lots of studies out there that suggest physical activity can prolong a person's lifespan and delay aging in various organs, such as the brain or the heart.
paras.zh: 如今，有大量研究表明体力活动可以延长人的寿命并延缓大脑或心脏等各个器官的衰老。

paras.en: But the health effects of exercise on the ovary are not nearly as well studied.
paras.zh: 但运动对卵巢健康的影响还没有得到充分研究。

paras.en: These new experiments among mice suggest that physical activity really can be a way to slow ovarian aging, and knowing more about the details has revealed a possible new drug target.
paras.zh: 这些在老鼠身上进行的新实验表明，体力活动确实可以成为减缓卵巢衰老的一种方法，并且了解更多细节已经揭示了一个可能的新药物靶点。

paras.en: "Although our animal experiments support causality, they might not fully recapitulate human ovarian aging," some of the team warn in a research briefing.
paras.zh: 研究小组的一些成员在研究简报中警告说：“尽管我们的动物实验支持因果关系，但它们可能无法完全重现人类卵巢衰老。”

paras.en: "We cannot definitively claim that physical activity prevents menopause…"
paras.zh: “我们不能明确地说体力活动可以预防更年期……”

paras.en: But what was found during these experiments is worth investigating further.
paras.zh: 但这些实验中的发现值得进一步研究。

paras.en: Especially since the study authors also found similar evidence in humans.
paras.zh: 特别是因为研究作者也在人类身上发现了类似的证据。

paras.en: In two large population studies, one from the UK and one from the US, premenopausal women reported higher physical activity levels than postmenopausal women.
paras.zh: 在两项大型人口研究（一项来自英国和一项来自美国）中，绝经前女性报告的体力活动水平高于绝经后女性。

paras.en: And in the UK study, higher physical activity levels were associated with a later age of menopause among postmenopausal individuals.
paras.zh: 在英国的研究中，绝经后个体较高的体力活动水平与较晚的绝经年龄有关。

paras.en: There was also another factor uniting the human evidence and the mouse evidence.
paras.zh: 还有另一个因素将人类证据和小鼠证据结合起来。

paras.en: Mice that were physically active on a treadmill showed increased levels of a protein hormone called adiponectin in their ovaries.
paras.zh: 在跑步机上进行体力活动的小鼠的卵巢中一种名为脂联素的蛋白质激素水平升高。

paras.en: This peptide is closely linked to the development of ovarian follicles and ovarian reserve.
paras.zh: 这种肽与卵泡的发育和卵巢储备功能密切相关。

paras.en: When female mice were given AdipoRon, a drug that stimulates adiponectin receptors, it extended their reproductive lifespan.
paras.zh: 当雌性小鼠服用 AdipoRon（一种刺激脂联素受体的药物）时，它们的生殖寿命得以延长。

paras.en: But when researchers reduced adiponectin production in the ovaries of mice, exercise's protective effect against primordial follicle loss fell by 76 percent.
paras.zh: 但当研究人员减少小鼠卵巢中脂联素的产生时，运动对原始卵泡损失的保护作用下降了 76%。

paras.en: When researchers turned to humans, they found a similar mechanistic link.
paras.zh: 当研究人员转向人类时，他们发现了类似的机制联系。

paras.en: Among nearly 147,000 participants in the UK Biobank, those carrying either of two genetic variants linked to adiponectin tended to experience menopause about a month later compared to the rest of the cohort.
paras.zh: 在英国生物银行的近 147,000 名参与者中，那些携带与脂联素相关的两种基因变异中的任何一种的人往往比其他人晚大约一个月经历更年期。

paras.en: "In this study, we provided substantial evidence that adiponectin functions as a primary, albeit not exclusive, mediator of the beneficial effects of physical activity," the team concludes.
paras.zh: 研究小组总结道：“在这项研究中，我们提供了大量证据，证明脂联素是体力活动有益影响的主要调节剂，尽管不是唯一的。”

paras.en: "Both physical activity and adiponectin may serve as promising targets for delaying ovarian aging, with substantial implications for both reproductive health and longevity."
paras.zh: “体力活动和脂联素都可能成为延缓卵巢衰老的有希望的目标，对生殖健康和长寿具有重大影响。”

paras.en: But first we need longer-term studies and randomized trials to put exercise interventions and AdipoRon to the test.
paras.zh: 但首先我们需要长期研究和随机试验来测试运动干预和 AdipoRon。

paras.en: AdipoRon is still in the preclinical phase, and more findings are needed before it can advance to human clinical trials.
paras.zh: AdipoRon 仍处于临床前阶段，需要更多研究结果才能进入人体临床试验。

paras.en: Still, given that adiponectin is not just present in the ovaries, there's reason to suspect that this drug may have broader longevity applications.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，鉴于脂联素不仅仅存在于卵巢中，我们有理由怀疑这种药物可能具有更广泛的长寿应用。

paras.en: "The mechanisms that regulate ovarian aging and female infertility are not well understood," says Scherer in a research briefing for Nature Aging.
paras.zh: “调节卵巢衰老和女性不孕的机制尚不清楚，”谢勒在《自然衰老》的研究简报中说。

paras.en: "This is particularly relevant today as more women delay childbirth into their late 30s, making interventions that preserve ovarian function increasingly important."
paras.zh: “这在今天尤其重要，因为越来越多的女性将生育推迟到 30 多岁，使得保护卵巢功能的干预措施变得越来越重要。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Aging.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然衰老》杂志上。

articles.title: Mole Rats Get Stressed When Earth's Magnetic Field Vanishes, Study Suggests
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: The amazing animal known as Ansell's mole rat (Fukomys anselli) is one of evolution's most interesting offerings: half fuzzy sausage and half Nemesis from Resident Evil.
paras.zh: 这种被称为安塞尔鼹鼠（Fukomys anselli）的神奇动物是进化中最有趣的产品之一：一半是毛茸茸的香肠，一半是《生化危机》中的复仇女神。

paras.en: This social, chonky creature 'sees' magnetic fields with its near-blind eyes to navigate its hand-dug, kilometers-long subterranean tunnels; the longest built by any mammal, save ourselves.
paras.zh: 这种社会性的、粗壮的生物用它近乎失明的眼睛“看到”磁场，从而在其手工挖掘的、长达数公里的地下隧道中导航；哺乳动物中最长的，拯救我们自己。

paras.en: Now, unique new research shows that this mole rat is so magnetically attuned that it shows signs of stress when Earth's guiding magnetic field nearly disappears – as any disaster movie connoisseur can understand.
paras.zh: 现在，独特的新研究表明，这种鼹鼠的磁力调节能力非常强，当地球引导磁场几乎消失时，它会表现出压力迹象——正如任何灾难电影鉴赏家都能理解的那样。

paras.en: The animal's amazing magnetosensation is still poorly understood, so a team led by neurobiologists from the Max Planck Institute for Neurobiology of Behavior used a new method to map the mole rats' brains to see how their neurons responded to magnetic field fluctuations.
paras.zh: 人们对这种动物惊人的磁感应能力仍然知之甚少，因此由马克斯·普朗克行为神经生物学研究所的神经生物学家领导的团队使用了一种新方法来绘制鼹鼠的大脑图，以了解它们的神经元如何对磁场波动做出反应。

paras.en: "We show here, to our knowledge, for the first time, that a mammal shows an active avoidance reaction to the absence of a magnetic field," the researchers explain in a preprint uploaded to bioRxiv.
paras.zh: 研究人员在上传到 bioRxiv 的预印本中解释说：“据我们所知，我们在这里首次证明哺乳动物在没有磁场的情况下表现出积极的回避反应。”

paras.en: Magnetic navigation has been mostly studied in migratory birds, which traverse large swathes of land and sea, but some mammals are also magnetically inclined.
paras.zh: 磁导航主要在候鸟身上进行研究，候鸟会穿越大片陆地和海洋，但一些哺乳动物也有磁倾向。

paras.en: Intriguingly, even dogs and some primates have a molecule in their eyes that, in birds, seems to react to magnetic fields when stimulated by light, according to past Max Planck research.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，根据马克斯·普朗克过去的研究，即使是狗和一些灵长类动物的眼睛里也有一种分子，而鸟类在受到光刺激时似乎会对磁场做出反应。

paras.en: But studies on magnetosensory brain areas in mammals have been limited to a single species, the subterranean Ansell's mole rat, the researchers note.
paras.zh: 但研究人员指出，对哺乳动物磁感应大脑区域的研究仅限于单一物种，即地下安塞尔鼹鼠。

paras.en: Oddly, previous research has found that numbing the surface of these animals' eyes with a local anesthetic robs them of their ability to build nests in their preferred compass direction, without robbing them of their limited ability to sense light.
paras.zh: 奇怪的是，之前的研究发现，用局部麻醉剂麻醉这些动物的眼睛表面，会剥夺它们在它们喜欢的指南针方向上筑巢的能力，但不会剥夺它们有限的感知光线的能力。

paras.en: So the researchers developed an imaging pipeline that used a chemical-based procedure to make the mole rats' brains transparent, creating a 3D map, or brain atlas.
paras.zh: 因此，研究人员开发了一种成像管道，使用基于化学的程序使鼹鼠的大脑变得透明，从而创建 3D 地图或大脑图谱。

paras.en: To evaluate the accuracy of their atlas, they then injected a fluorescent tracer into the eyes of living mole rats to label the neural wiring and structural connections across the visual-brain pathway and overlay it onto their atlas.
paras.zh: 为了评估地图集的准确性，他们将荧光示踪剂注射到活鼹鼠的眼睛中，以标记视觉大脑通路上的神经线路和结构连接，并将其覆盖到地图集上。

paras.en: Experimentally, they subjected mole rats to a changing magnetic field (CMF) and a near-zero hypomagnetic field (HMF), the latter of which was around 2 percent of the intensity of Earth's magnetic field in Germany, where the tests were conducted.
paras.zh: 在实验中，他们将鼹鼠置于变化的磁场 (CMF) 和近零低磁场 (HMF) 中，后者的强度约为德国地球磁场强度的 2%。

paras.en: Every 30 seconds, the CMF changed either only in orientation or in both orientation and intensity, ranging from 20 to 70 times the strength of the near-zero field.
paras.zh: 每 30 秒，CMF 要么仅改变方向，要么改变方向和强度，范围为近零场强度的 20 至 70 倍。

paras.en: Surprisingly, the most robust and widespread brain response occurred in the presence of the HMF – in other words, a lack of stimulus proved the most salient stimulus.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，最强烈和最广泛的大脑反应发生在 HMF 存在的情况下——换句话说，缺乏刺激被证明是最显着的刺激。

paras.en: The mole rats exposed to the HMF displayed higher brain activity in regions linked to stress, anxiety, and fear, including the almond-shaped amygdala, which is also associated with decision-making and emotional processing.
paras.zh: 接触 HMF 的鼹鼠在与压力、焦虑和恐惧相关的区域表现出更高的大脑活动，包括杏仁状的杏仁核，它也与决策和情绪处理有关。

paras.en: Therefore, even though the near-absence of a magnetic field was expected to result in a neutral state, perhaps akin to a human perplexedly staring at a roadmap, it instead triggered brain activity resembling a stress response.
paras.zh: 因此，尽管几乎没有磁场预计会导致中性状态，也许类似于人类困惑地盯着路线图，但它反而触发了类似于压力反应的大脑活动。

paras.en: "Based on the neural activation patterns indicative of a stress-like state induced by HMF exposure, we hypothesized that mole rats perceive the lack of a magnetic field as aversive and consequently exhibit active avoidance behavior to HMF," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“根据表明 HMF 暴露引起的类似压力状态的神经激活模式，我们假设鼹鼠将缺乏磁场视为厌恶，从而对 HMF 表现出主动回避行为。”

paras.en: The same results manifested in a second experiment.
paras.zh: 第二个实验也出现了相同的结果。

paras.en: Mole rats were placed in a linear track wherein the researchers created a local magnetic-field anomaly by varying the magnetic intensity based on the animal's position. They spent significantly less time near an object placed inside the near-zero zone. Doubling the field strength had no such effect.
paras.zh: 鼹鼠被放置在一条直线轨道上，研究人员根据动物的位置改变磁场强度，从而产生局部磁场异常。他们在接近零区域内的物体附近花费的时间明显减少。将场强加倍没有这样的效果。

paras.en: But how mole rats sense magnetic fields is still an open question.
paras.zh: 但鼹鼠如何感知磁场仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

paras.en: In fact, it may be more open than ever, as a recently published paper in the journal iScience reports no evidence for the naturally magnetic magnetite-based receptors thought to exist in mole-rat eyes, like little lodestones.
paras.zh: 事实上，它可能比以往任何时候都更加开放，因为《iScience》杂志最近发表的一篇论文报告称，没有证据表明鼹鼠眼睛中存在天然磁性的磁铁矿受体，就像小磁石一样。

paras.en: Further muddying the matter, this research links the mole rats' magnetic intuitions to a wide distribution of brain regions and circuitry, rather than a simple 'fridge magnet' neural center.
paras.zh: 这项研究将鼹鼠的磁性直觉与广泛分布的大脑区域和电路联系起来，而不是简单的“冰箱磁石”神经中枢，这让事情变得更加混乱。

paras.en: Yet this study's novel imaging pipeline could provide a framework for future magnetosensation studies in mole rats and other animals – perhaps very, very many animals.
paras.zh: 然而，这项研究的新颖成像流程可以为未来对鼹鼠和其他动物（也许是非常非常多的动物）的磁感应研究提供一个框架。

paras.en: It also importantly reveals that near-zero magnetic fields may no longer provide useful controls in such studies, especially with mole rats, as they may stress the animals being tested.
paras.zh: 它还重要地表明，接近零的磁场可能不再在此类研究中提供有用的控制，特别是对于鼹鼠，因为它们可能会给被测试的动物带来压力。

paras.en: "In summary, we present evidence that mole rats perceive the absence of the Earth's magnetic field," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“总之，我们提供的证据表明鼹鼠感知到地球磁场的缺失。”

paras.en: "We show that the removal of this normally constant environmental stimulus, the Earth's magnetic field, activates stress-related brain circuits and triggers active avoidance behavior."
paras.zh: “我们表明，消除这种通常持续的环境刺激（地球磁场）会激活与压力相关的大脑回路并引发主动回避行为。”

paras.en: Had evolution taken a different twist, might the previously mentioned magnetic receptor remnants in primate eyes have bloomed and allowed people to (just as begrudgingly) find their way to work every morning along our planet's magnetic field? Who knows.
paras.zh: 如果进化发生了不同的转变，前面提到的灵长类动物眼睛中的磁性受体残余物是否会大量繁殖，并允许人们（同样不情愿地）找到每天早上沿着地球磁场工作的方式？谁知道呢。

paras.en: "Our findings demonstrate that the Earth's magnetic field constitutes a biologically significant sensory stimulus in mammals," the team concludes.
paras.zh: 研究小组总结道：“我们的研究结果表明，地球磁场对哺乳动物构成了具有生物学意义的感官刺激。”

paras.en: The study has not yet been peer-reviewed, but a preprint is available on bioRxiv.
paras.zh: 该研究尚未经过同行评审，但预印本可在 bioRxiv 上找到。

articles.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist

paras.en: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
paras.zh: 剑桥科学家发明了一款价值 10 美元的芯片，可以将医学实验室放在你的手腕上

paras.en: - Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.
paras.zh: - 剑桥研究人员创造了一款突破性的 10 美元光学传感器，该传感器在一个足够小的可穿戴技术设备中提供实验室设备的精度。它在测试中以 100% 的准确度识别食品、塑料和药品，并展示了无需侵入性操作即可监测血糖、酒精和其他健康指标的能力。

paras.en: A new optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.
paras.zh: 一种成本仅为 10 美元的新型光学传感器可以为可穿戴健康监测器带来实验室级的精度，从而使人们无需针头即可追踪血糖。该技术还可以改变食品检测、工业质量控制和环境监测。

paras.en: Researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a new type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.
paras.zh: 剑桥大学和 GlitterinTech（同一研究小组创立的初创公司）的研究人员开发了一种新型光学光谱仪，该光谱仪将卓越的精度与非常小的尺寸和低成本结合在一起。该设备直径仅为厘米，可以集成到便携式电子产品和可穿戴健康技术中。其潜在应用范围从实时监测重要的健康标记到识别材料和检测化学成分的变化。

paras.en: Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.
paras.zh: 光谱仪通过分析光来揭示与其相互作用的物质的信息。它们是医学、制造、化学测试和环境研究的重要工具。然而，传统上，使这些仪器变得更小意味着牺牲它们的性能。紧凑型光谱仪通常测量范围有限、分辨率较低或精度较低，这使得它们比执行精确测量更适合识别物质。

paras.en: The researchers believe their new design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.
paras.zh: 研究人员相信他们的新设计可以克服这些限制。它被称为卷积光谱仪，它使用称为卷积定理的数学原理以根本不同的方式分析光。该团队表示，这种方法在几个关键领域的性能超越了现有类型的光谱仪，包括基于光色散、傅立叶变换和计算重建的设计。

paras.en: A New Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision
paras.zh: 一种以非凡精度分析光的新方法

paras.en: Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The new device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.
paras.zh: 传统的光谱仪通常将入射光分成其组成波长或使用复杂的计算来重建其光谱。新设备采用了另一种方法，直接对入射光执行称为卷积的数学运算。

paras.en: To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.
paras.zh: 为了实现这一目标，研究人员按顺序排列了具有重复光谱响应的光学元件。这些组件可以包括不平衡马赫-曾德尔干涉仪或微环谐振器。通过按比例调整它们，系统可以以受控的线性方式将其响应转移到不同的波长。然后使用快速傅里叶变换来准确地恢复光谱。

paras.en: "The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," said Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system."
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者姚春辉博士说：“关键的见解是回到数学并询问是否有一种从根本上更清洁的方法来检索光谱。” “通过直接在光域中使用卷积定理，我们避免了许多阻碍小型化光谱仪的限制。这为我们提供了高精度、强噪声容限和非常低的计算开销，所有这些都在一个紧凑且低成本的系统中。”

paras.en: The researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.
paras.zh: 研究人员使用氮化硅光子平台构建了光谱仪，并将其与机载电子设备集成。它在广泛的近红外波长（1200-1700 nm）范围内工作，可以在不到一秒的时间内收集和处理测量结果。

paras.en: Another important advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.
paras.zh: 另一个重要优势是它能够在不进行重大硬件更改的情况下扩展其测量功能。由于该系统使用重复的光学图案，因此理论上其光谱带宽几乎可以无限扩展。依次添加更多的光学元件也可以成倍地提高其分辨率。

paras.en: A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare
paras.zh: 10 美元的传感器可以改变食品检测和医疗保健

paras.en: To evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.
paras.zh: 为了在纯理论测量之外评估该设备，研究人员在各种材料和物质上对其进行了测试。结果证明了它在通常依赖于更大、更昂贵的实验室仪器的应用中的潜力。

paras.en: When used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.
paras.zh: 当用于识别塑料、药品、咖啡、面粉和茶时，该光谱仪在报告的测试中实现了 100% 的分类成功率。它还测量水基和有机溶液中的浓度，精度约为 0.01%，超过了这些实验中商用台式光谱仪的性能。

paras.en: The healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.
paras.zh: 医疗保健示威特别有希望。在反映真实生理环境的条件下，该设备准确测量了多种人体生物标志物，包括皮肤湿度、血液酒精、血乳酸和血糖。

paras.en: The researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.
paras.zh: 研究人员还对一名参与者进行了长时间的无创血糖追踪。尽管该技术在成为实用的医疗产品之前还需要进行进一步的测试，但这一发现表明了一种无需反复刺穿皮肤即可监测血糖的可能途径。

paras.en: "These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," said Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment."
paras.zh: “这些生物医学演示特别令人兴奋，”该项目负责人程启祥教授说。 “这项工作的脱颖而出不仅在于实验室的表现，还在于技术准备。姚春辉博士的贡献对于将数学概念转化为完整封装的、强大的系统至关重要，该系统可以在极端温度和现实条件下可靠运行。这种结合为实际部署打开了大门。”

paras.en: The sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.
paras.zh: 该传感器还表现出令人印象深刻的抗温度变化能力。它在 -20°C 至 80°C 之间持续可靠运行，这对于微型光谱仪来说是一个异常宽的温度范围。这种耐用性对于可穿戴设备、工厂设备和户外运行的传感器尤其有价值。

paras.en: Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough
paras.zh: 为什么更简单的设计可能是一个重大突破

paras.en: The new spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.
paras.zh: 新型光谱仪的优势不仅仅在于精度、尺寸和价格。其内部设计还减少了分析入射光所需的计算能力。

paras.en: Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.
paras.zh: 许多现有的微型光谱仪依赖复杂的校准程序和苛刻的算法来重建光谱信息。当测量结果包含噪声时，这些方法可能变得不可靠，并且通常需要大量的处理资源。

paras.en: The Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.
paras.zh: 剑桥团队基于卷积的方法避免了大部分这种复杂性。由于测量遵循线性数学关系，因此系统可以快速一致地恢复光谱，同时使用相对较少的计算能力。

paras.en: "This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," said Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible."
paras.zh: “这是一个美丽的例子，展示了优雅的工程如何释放真正的影响，”为光子系统设计和集成做出贡献的理查德·彭蒂教授说。 “该架构简单、可扩展且可制造，但其精度可与大型仪器相媲美或超过。姚春辉博士在将光子设计、系统集成和实验验证结合在一起方面发挥了核心作用，使这成为可能。”

paras.en: Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.
paras.zh: 其相对简单的结构还可以使该技术更容易大规模制造，从而有可能为传统光谱仪过于笨重或昂贵的设备带来复杂的光学测量。

paras.en: Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices
paras.zh: 将实验室级测量引入日常设备

paras.en: The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.
paras.zh: 研究人员设想，未来精确的光学传感将成为日常技术的常规特征，而不再主要局限于专业实验室。

paras.en: In industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is currently practical.
paras.zh: 在工业环境中，可以在整个制造设施中安装廉价的光谱仪，以持续检查材料成分和产品质量。类似的传感器可以在比目前实际规模大得多的范围内监测食品新鲜度、识别物质并分析环境条件。

paras.en: Healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.
paras.zh: 医疗保健也可能发生同样重大的变化。紧凑型传感器最终可能使可穿戴设备能够测量水合水平，检测酒精中毒的迹象，跟踪与身体健康相关的生物标志物，或持续监测糖尿病患者的血糖水平。

paras.en: "Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work shows that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day."
paras.zh: “我们的愿景是让光谱测量像温度或运动传感一样无处不在，”程启祥教授补充道。 “这项工作表明，高质量的光谱信息不必局限于实验室——它可以直接嵌入到人们每天使用的技术中。”

paras.en: As photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a new generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.
paras.zh: 随着光子技术变得更小、更先进，卷积光谱仪提供了一个有希望的例子，说明数学见解和实际工程如何使复杂的科学仪器变得更简单、更便宜、更容易使用。通过将高精度与成本约为 10 美元的设备相结合，研究人员为新一代智能传感器开辟了一条潜在途径，能够测量我们身体和周围环境中隐藏的化学成分。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Original written by Michael Shuff. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由剑桥大学提供。原创作者：迈克尔·舒夫。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Chunhui Yao, Jie Ma, Ningning Wang, Peng Bao, Wei Zhuo, Tao Zhang, Wanlu Zhang, Kangning Xu, Ting Yan, Liang Ming, Yuxiao Ye, Tawfique Hasan, Ian White, Richard Penty, Qixiang Cheng. Optical convolutional spectrometer. Nature Photonics, 2026; 20 (6): 664 DOI: 10.1038/s41566-026-01891-6
paras.zh: - 姚春辉、马杰、王宁宁、鲍鹏、卓伟、张涛、张万禄、徐康宁、严婷、梁明、叶雨晓、Tawfique Hasan、Ian White、Richard Penty、Qiyang Cheng。光学卷积光谱仪。自然光子学，2026； 20 (6): 664 DOI: 10.1038/s41566-026-01891-6

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe

paras.en: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
paras.zh: 近 3,000 颗爆炸的恒星挑战着我们对宇宙的理解

paras.en: - A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universeâs expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
paras.zh: - 对 2,884 颗爆炸恒星的大规模分析发现了新的证据，表明暗能量（加速宇宙膨胀的神秘力量）可能会随着时间的推移而发生变化。这些发现挑战了现代宇宙学的基石，并可能重塑我们对宇宙如何运作的理解。

paras.en: The largest collection of exploding white dwarf stars ever compiled is providing fresh evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force responsible for the Universe’s accelerating expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a central assumption of modern cosmology and could help scientists better understand how the Universe evolves.
paras.zh: 迄今为止最大的爆炸白矮星集合提供了新的证据，表明暗能量（导致宇宙加速膨胀的神秘力量）可能会随着时间的推移而发生变化。这些发现挑战了现代宇宙学的一个中心假设，可以帮助科学家更好地理解宇宙是如何演化的。

paras.en: An international research team led by scientists at the University of Queensland’s School of Mathematics and Physics brought together observations of 2,884 Type Ia supernovae. These powerful stellar explosions serve as important tools for measuring distances across the Universe, allowing astronomers to trace its expansion history.
paras.zh: 由昆士兰大学数学与物理学院科学家领导的国际研究小组汇集了对 2,884 颗 Ia 型超新星的观测结果。这些强大的恒星爆炸是测量宇宙距离的重要工具，使天文学家能够追踪其膨胀历史。

paras.en: PhD candidate Ryan Camilleri said the project establishes a new international standard for supernova cosmology. By bringing decades of measurements into a unified dataset, researchers have created their most detailed picture yet of how cosmic expansion has changed over time.
paras.zh: 博士生瑞安·卡米莱里 (Ryan Camilleri) 表示，该项目为超新星宇宙学建立了新的国际标准。通过将数十年的测量结果纳入统一的数据集中，研究人员创建了迄今为止最详细的图像，展示了宇宙膨胀如何随时间变化。

paras.en: “We’ve rebuilt 3 decades of astronomical observations into a single, consistent framework,” Mr. Camilleri said.
paras.zh: “我们将 3 年的天文观测重建为一个单一、一致的框架，”卡米莱里先生说。

paras.en: “We combined our data with other cosmic measurements including relic light from the Big Bang and maps of how galaxies are distributed through space.
paras.zh: “我们将我们的数据与其他宇宙测量数据结合起来，包括大爆炸的遗迹光和星系在空间中如何分布的地图。

paras.en: “Instead of confirming the standard model of cosmology which assumes dark energy is fixed and unchanging, we have more evidence that dark energy may change over time.”
paras.zh: “我们没有证实宇宙学的标准模型假设暗能量是固定不变的，而是有更多证据表明暗能量可能会随着时间的推移而变化。”

paras.en: Combining Three Decades of Supernova Observations
paras.zh: 结合三个十年的超新星观测

paras.en: The new collection brings together historical supernova measurements and findings from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) published in 2024.
paras.zh: 新合集汇集了历史上的超新星测量结果和 2024 年发布的暗能量巡天 (DES) 的发现。

paras.en: To make observations collected over different periods directly comparable, the scientists revisited older data using updated analytical methods. Advances in understanding supernova behavior allowed the team to improve the consistency and accuracy of measurements gathered over decades.
paras.zh: 为了使不同时期收集的观测结果具有直接可比性，科学家们使用更新的分析方法重新审视了旧数据。对超新星行为理解的进步使团队能够提高数十年来收集的测量结果的一致性和准确性。

paras.en: “Over the years we’ve learned a lot more about how supernovae behave so we’ve been able to go back and apply that improved understanding to older data,” Mr. Camilleri said.
paras.zh: 卡米莱里先生说：“多年来，我们对超新星的行为有了更多了解，因此我们能够回过头来，将加深的理解应用于旧数据。”

paras.en: The researchers also had to account for differences among the telescopes used to collect the observations. Other factors, including cosmic dust and the masses of galaxies, can influence the light astronomers receive from distant supernovae and therefore affect distance measurements.
paras.zh: 研究人员还必须考虑用于收集观测结果的望远镜之间的差异。其他因素，包括宇宙尘埃和星系质量，可能会影响天文学家从遥远的超新星接收到的光，从而影​​响距离测量。

paras.en: “Extensive work has been done to link observations from different telescopes with different capacities and take into account issues such as cosmic dust and galaxy mass which can affect the light coming from a supernova.
paras.zh: “我们已经开展了大量工作，将具有不同能力的不同望远镜的观测结果联系起来，并考虑到宇宙尘埃和星系质量等可能影响超新星发出的光的问题。

paras.en: “We also incorporated more subtle effects such as gravitational lensing, which is the bending and magnification of light around large objects as it travels from a supernova to Earth.”
paras.zh: “我们还融入了更微妙的效果，例如引力透镜，这是大型物体周围的光从超新星传播到地球时的弯曲和放大。”

paras.en: New Evidence Challenges the Dark Energy Model
paras.zh: 新证据挑战暗能量模型

paras.en: Astrophysicist Professor Tamara Davis said the expanded dataset represents an important advance in efforts to understand the nature of dark energy.
paras.zh: 天体物理学家塔玛拉·戴维斯教授表示，扩展的数据集代表了理解暗能量本质的重要进展。

paras.en: Under the standard model of cosmology, dark energy is treated as a constant property of the Universe. However, recent observations have raised questions about whether that assumption fully explains how cosmic expansion has evolved.
paras.zh: 在宇宙学的标准模型下，暗能量被视为宇宙的恒定属性。然而，最近的观察提出了这样的问题：这一假设是否充分解释了宇宙膨胀是如何演化的。

paras.en: “Our supernova data from DES in 2024 first showed hints that dark energy may be time varying, and this new compilation also sees a deviation from the standard model although in a slightly different direction,” Professor Davis said.
paras.zh: 戴维斯教授说：“我们在 2024 年从 DES 获得的超新星数据首次显示暗能量可能随时间变化的暗示，而这个新的汇编也看到了与标准模型的偏差，尽管方向略有不同。”

paras.en: The findings are especially interesting because a separate astronomical project has also produced evidence suggesting that dark energy might not remain constant.
paras.zh: 这些发现特别有趣，因为一个单独的天文项目也产生了证据表明暗能量可能不会保持恒定。

paras.en: “Similarly results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) found hints of variations in dark energy in its surveys of relic sound waves from the early Universe.
paras.zh: “暗能量光谱仪（DESI）的类似结果在对早期宇宙遗迹声波的调查中发现了暗能量变化的迹象。

paras.en: “So, 2 completely independent measurements have found hints of time variation in dark energy, challenging the standard model that dark energy doesn't change.
paras.zh: “因此，两次完全独立的测量发现了暗能量随时间变化的迹象，挑战了暗能量不会改变的标准模型。

paras.en: Although the different measurements do not point to exactly the same departure from the standard model, they provide additional reasons to investigate whether dark energy changes as the Universe ages.
paras.zh: 尽管不同的测量结果并不表明与标准模型的偏离完全相同，但它们为研究暗能量是否随着宇宙老化而变化提供了额外的理由。

paras.en: Could Dark Energy Help Unite Gravity and Quantum Physics?
paras.zh: 暗能量可以帮助统一引力和量子物理学吗？

paras.en: Understanding dark energy could have implications extending far beyond the expansion of the Universe. Researchers believe that learning more about its behavior might also provide insights into one of the greatest unresolved problems in theoretical physics: reconciling gravity with quantum physics.
paras.zh: 了解暗能量的影响可能远远超出宇宙的膨胀范围。研究人员认为，更多地了解其行为也可能有助于深入了解理论物理学中尚未解决的最大问题之一：协调引力与量子物理学。

paras.en: “All of this research may also hold the clue to explain how gravity and quantum physics fit together.
paras.zh: “所有这些研究也可能为解释引力和量子物理学如何结合在一起提供线索。

paras.en: “We know these 2 theories are each immensely successful in their own realms, so if we can figure out how to put them together that would be a huge step in theoretical physics.”
paras.zh: “我们知道这两种理论在各自的领域都取得了巨大的成功，因此，如果我们能够弄清楚如何将它们结合在一起，那将是理论物理学的一大进步。”

paras.en: Future Supernova Surveys Could Provide More Answers
paras.zh: 未来的超新星巡天可以提供更多答案

paras.en: The researchers plan to expand the dataset as additional observations become available. One important source will be the Dark Energy Bedrock All-Sky Supernova program (DEBASS), which is identifying hundreds of supernovae at distances closer to Earth than those surveyed by DES.
paras.zh: 研究人员计划随着更多观察结果的出现而扩展数据集。暗能量基岩全天超新星计划 (DEBASS) 是一个重要来源，该计划正在识别数百颗超新星，其距离地球的距离比 DES 调查的距离更近。

paras.en: Incorporating these nearby explosions will provide further measurements that scientists can use to investigate the Universe’s expansion and test whether dark energy truly changes over time.
paras.zh: 结合这些附近的爆炸将提供进一步的测量结果，科学家们可以利用这些测量结果来研究宇宙的膨胀并测试暗能量是否真正随着时间的推移而变化。
